definition_zh: 使发笑；逗乐；给……提供消遣
definition_en: to make someone laugh or smile, or to keep someone pleasantly occupied
core_image: 候车室里，一个孩子用纸折出小动物逗弟弟笑
scene: 长途车上，邻座的人讲了几个笑话，把整排乘客都逗笑了。 The jokes amused the tired passengers.
sceneCN: 这里 amuse 是「逗乐；使发笑」（第 1 个义项：让人笑起来）；句意是这些笑话把疲惫的乘客逗乐了。

pos.zh: 动词：使发笑；逗乐；给……消遣

derivatives.zh: 名词：娱乐；消遣；乐趣
形容词：有趣的；逗人笑的
形容词：被逗乐的
副词：有趣地

senses.title: To make someone laugh
senses.definition: to cause someone to laugh or smile, usually with something funny
senses.definitionCN: 用有趣的东西让人发笑或微笑
senses.example: The jokes amused the tired passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些笑话把疲惫的乘客逗乐了。
senses.why: The word began in French with a sense of distracting or stupefying the mind, and laughter is the gentlest form of that distraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初在法语中意为分散注意、使头脑发懵，而笑声正是这种分神最温和的形式。

senses.title: To keep pleasantly occupied
senses.definition: to give someone something enjoyable to do so that time passes happily
senses.definitionCN: 给某人有趣的事情做，使时间愉快地过去
senses.example: The museum keeps children amused for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆能让孩子们开心地待上几个小时。
senses.why: Amusement need not be laughter; anything that holds attention pleasantly keeps the mind from boredom, which is the older sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 消遣不一定要有笑声；任何能愉快地占据注意力、使心思不落到无聊上的东西都算，这正是这个词较早的含义。

intro.en: Amuse originally meant to distract the mind, not to make it laugh.
intro.cn: amuse 最初指分散心思，而不是让人发笑。

items.en: muser meant 'to stare, to ponder, to waste time', the base of the word.
items.cn: muser 意为「呆看、沉思、消磨时间」，是该词的词基。

items.en: amuser meant 'to deceive, to stupefy, to divert attention'.
items.cn: amuser 意为「欺骗、使发懵、转移注意力」。

items.en: English amuse first meant 'to divert the attention, to occupy'.
items.cn: 英语 amuse 最初意为「转移注意力、使忙碌」。

items.en: The sense narrowed towards pleasant diversion and then to making people laugh.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄为愉快的消遣，随后又指逗人发笑。

items.en: Amusing now usually means funny, while amusement covers both laughter and pastime.
items.cn: 如今 amusing 通常指好笑，而 amusement 既指笑也指消遣。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the muse base; the near-meaning group grades entertainment.
note.cn: 形近组共享 muse 词基；近义组按娱乐方式分级。

normalIntro.en: Amuse is a-muse: to lead the mind away from boredom.
normalIntro.cn: amuse 可看作 a 加 muse：把心思从无聊中引开。

normal.en: Muse means to ponder; amuse first meant to distract.
normal.cn: muse 意为沉思，amuse 最初意为分散注意。

normal.en: Amusing is the adjective for something funny.
normal.cn: amusing 是形容某物好笑的形容词。

normal.en: Be amused by, not amused from.
normal.cn: 搭配是 be amused by，不用 from。

normal.en: An amusement park is a place of pastime.
normal.cn: amusement park 是消遣之地。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-MUSE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-MUSE。

abstract.en: Picture a paper animal folded on a bus.
abstract.cn: 想象在公交车上折出的纸动物。

abstract.en: See a row of passengers smiling at a joke.
abstract.cn: 想象一排乘客被笑话逗笑。

abstract.en: Imagine a child busy for hours in a museum.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在博物馆里玩上几个小时。

examples.en: The clown amused the children for an hour.
examples.cn: 小丑逗孩子们开心了一个小时。

examples.en: I was amused by his imitation of the teacher.
examples.cn: 他模仿老师的样子把我逗乐了。

examples.en: She amused herself by reading old letters.
examples.cn: 她读旧信来消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: a 加 muse（沉思）：把沉思的人拉出来，就是逗乐、消遣。

root: 源自古法语 amuser「欺骗、使发懵、转移注意」，其词基 muser 意为呆看、沉思；十五世纪进入英语时意为转移注意力，十七世纪渐指愉快的消遣，现代更常指逗人发笑。

sensesIntro.en: Diverting the mind yields two uses: provoking laughter and filling time pleasantly.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把心思引开」生出两种用法：引人发笑，以及愉快地打发时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded paper animal making a child smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：折纸小动物逗笑孩子。

branches.cn: 长途车上的笑话

branches.en: a clown working a crowd
branches.cn: 逗笑观众的小丑

branches.en: a museum that occupies children
branches.cn: 让孩子有事可做的博物馆

branches.en: reading old letters to pass time
branches.cn: 读旧信打发时间

branches.en: games that keep guests happy

intro.en: A French verb with a compact English family around amusement.
intro.cn: 这是法语动词，英语中围绕 amusement 有一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自法语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 整齐的；有条理的；有秩序的；勤务兵；医院勤杂工
definition_en: neatly arranged and well organized; calm and behaving properly; also a soldier who carries orders or an attendant who does routine jobs in a hospital
core_image: 推车上的药瓶沿桌沿站成一条直线，标签全都朝外
scene: 病房晨间查房前，一个穿制服的人把推车上的药瓶按床号排成一条直线。 The medical orderly arranged the trays in a neat row before the doctor arrived.
sceneCN: 这里是「医院勤杂工」（第 4 个义项：在医院做杂务、协助护理的人）；句意为医生到之前，他把托盘摆得整整齐齐。图中可辨识物件：药瓶、推车、制服。

pos.zh: 整齐的；有条理的；有秩序的

derivatives.zh: 由 orderly 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「整洁；井然有序」
语源上的基础词，义为「顺序；秩序；命令」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 orderly 构成，义为「混乱的；妨害治安的」

senses.title: Neatly arranged
senses.definition: arranged in a neat and well-organized way, with everything in its proper place
senses.definitionCN: 摆放整齐、安排有条理，每样东西都在该在的位置
senses.example: She keeps her notes in orderly piles on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她把笔记在桌上摞得整整齐齐。
senses.why: The adjective is order plus -ly in its old sense of having the quality of, so anything orderly visibly carries the pattern of an arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词是 order 加 -ly，这里的 -ly 是「具有……性质」的旧用法，所以 orderly 的东西身上看得出被安排过的痕迹。

senses.title: Peaceful and well-behaved
senses.definition: calm and controlled, with people behaving properly and without confusion
senses.definitionCN: 平静而有节制，人们举止得当、不慌乱
senses.example: The crowd was orderly as it filed through the gates.
senses.exampleCN: 人群排队通过大门时井然有序。
senses.why: A crowd that keeps its lines shows the same outer pattern as a tidy shelf, so the word moves from objects to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 排队不乱的队伍，外表上和整齐的搁架有同一种纹路，于是这个词就从物件挪到了举止。

senses.title: A soldier who carries orders
senses.definition: a soldier whose job is to carry orders, messages or supplies for an officer or a unit
senses.definitionCN: 为军官或部队传递命令、信件或补给品的士兵
senses.example: An orderly brought the captain's sealed orders before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前，一名勤务兵送来了上尉的密封命令。
senses.why: In an army the person who moves orders from one place to another is named after the orders themselves, so the adjective for in order became a job title.
senses.whyCN: 在军队里，把命令从一处送到另一处的人，直接拿「命令」来命名，于是表示「有秩序」的形容词成了岗位名。

senses.title: An attendant in a hospital
senses.definition: a hospital worker who does routine tasks such as moving patients, supplies and records
senses.definitionCN: 在医院里搬送病人、物品和病历等杂务的工作人员
senses.example: The orderly wheeled the trolley past the crowded ward.
senses.exampleCN: 那名杂工推着推车穿过拥挤的病房。
senses.why: The military title crossed into hospitals, where the person who keeps the ward's daily routine in order took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这个军队里的称呼也进了医院：负责让病房日常运转不乱的人，沿用同一个名字。

intro.en: Orderly is an English construction from order plus -ly, and order itself came from Latin through French.
intro.cn: orderly 是英语用 order 加 -ly 造出来的词，而 order 本身经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Latin ordo named a row, a line or a fixed arrangement, and its genitive ordinis is the stem behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ordo 指一排、一行或固定的次序，属格 ordinis 是整个词族的词干。

items.en: The verb ordinare meant to set in order or to arrange, and it kept the family close to the idea of putting things in rows.
items.cn: 动词 ordinare 意为「排好、安排」，让这一族词始终贴近「把东西排成行」的意思。

items.en: Old French ordre carried both arrangement and command, and English borrowed it as order.
items.cn: 古法语 ordre 同时带有「安排」与「命令」两层意思，英语借入后写作 order。

items.en: English added -ly to order to make orderly, meaning having order or kept in order, and the noun sense appeared soon after.
items.cn: 英语给 order 加上 -ly 造出 orderly，意为「有次序的、被整理好的」，名词用法随后不久出现。

items.en: Modern English extended orderly to calm crowds, then to the soldier and the hospital worker who keep things running.
items.cn: 现代英语把 orderly 扩展到守秩序的队伍，再用来指维持秩序的士兵与医院杂工。

note.en: The look-alike group is the order family and its negated form; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for things kept in good arrangement.
note.cn: 形近组是 order 词族及其否定形式；近义组是表示「收拾得整齐」的形容词。

entries.definition: An arrangement, a sequence, or an instruction to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 安排、次序，或让人做某事的指示。

entries.definition: The quality of being neat and well arranged.
Untidy, noisy, or behaving in a way that breaks public order.
entries.definitionCN: 凌乱的、吵闹的，或扰乱公共秩序的。

entries.definition: Clean and arranged with care, with no mess.
Having everything in its right place.
entries.definitionCN: 每样东西都在合适位置的。

entries.definition: Done in a careful, step-by-step way.

normalIntro.en: Orderly is built from two ordinary English pieces, and its family keeps returning to the picture of things lined up and kept in place.
normalIntro.cn: orderly 由两个平常的英语部件构成，这一族词反复回到「东西排成行、各在其位」的画面。

normal.en: Orderly is order plus -ly, so the first meaning is simply having order.
normal.cn: orderly 是 order 加 -ly，所以第一层意思就是「有次序的」。

normal.en: Orderliness is the noun of the same word, naming the neatness itself.
normal.cn: orderliness 是同一个词的名词形式，把整洁本身当成一个东西来指。

normal.en: Disorderly adds dis- and reverses the picture into confusion and noise.
normal.cn: disorderly 加 dis-，把画面反过来，成了混乱与吵闹。

normal.en: In the army, the orderly is the one who carries orders from place to place.
normal.cn: 在军队里，orderly 就是把命令从一处送到另一处的人。

normal.en: A hospital orderly does the small jobs that keep a ward in order.
normal.cn: 医院里的 orderly 做的是让病房保持有序的那些杂事。

abstract.en: A line of bottles standing along the edge of a table: order you can see.
abstract.cn: 一排药瓶贴着桌沿站好：这是看得见的秩序。

abstract.en: The same word covers a tidy shelf, a calm crowd and a man carrying messages, because each is a pattern that holds.
abstract.cn: 同一个词罩住整齐的架子、安静的人群和送信的人，因为三者都是撑住的纹路。

abstract.en: Small repeated acts, not one great gesture, are what keep a ward or an army in order.
abstract.cn: 让病房或军队保持有序的，是许多重复的小动作，而不是一个大姿态。

examples.en: The medical orderly arranged the trays in a neat row before the doctor arrived.
examples.cn: 医生到之前，那名医院杂工把托盘摆成整齐的一排。

examples.en: The crowd was orderly as it filed through the gates.
examples.cn: 人群排队通过大门时井然有序。

examples.en: She keeps her notes in orderly piles on the desk.
examples.cn: 她把笔记在桌上摞得整整齐齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喔得利」——东西各归其位，收拾得利利索索；记住 orderly 是整齐的、有秩序的。

root: order 来自拉丁语 ordo（一排、次序，属格 ordinis）经古法语 ordre 进入英语；orderly 是 order 加形容词后缀 -ly，本义「有次序的」，再扩展到守秩序的人与岗位。同族词有 orderliness、disorderly。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a visible pattern that holds things in place; the senses go from arranged objects to calm behaviour, then to the soldier and the hospital worker who keep that pattern alive.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西固定住的可见纹路」；义项从摆好的物件走到安静的举止，再到维持这种纹路的士兵与医院杂工。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of bottles standing along the edge of a table, labels all facing out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排药瓶贴着桌沿站好，标签全都朝外。

branches.en: pill bottles standing along the edge of a table
branches.cn: 药瓶沿桌沿站成一列

branches.en: notes piled square on a desk
branches.cn: 笔记在桌上摞得方方正正

branches.en: a line of people waiting without pushing
branches.cn: 一队人不推不挤地等着

branches.en: a runner crossing a camp with a sealed message
branches.cn: 传令兵带着密封信件穿过营地

branches.en: a trolley rolled quietly past beds
branches.cn: 推车从病床旁轻轻推过

intro.en: The word is made of two English pieces, order and -ly, and the Latin stem behind order supplies the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个词由 order 与 -ly 两个英语部件构成，而 order 背后的拉丁词干提供了其余的同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is ordo, a row or a fixed arrangement, together with its genitive form and its adjective ordinarius.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 ordo（一排、固定的次序），以及它的属格形式和形容词 ordinarius。

definition_zh: 省略；遗漏；不提及；排除在外
definition_en: to leave something out on purpose, to fail to include it by mistake, to say nothing about it, or to keep someone or something off a list
core_image: 一张写好的名单上，中间一行被人用笔轻轻划掉，留下一道细线
scene: 办公室的灯还亮着，编辑把打印稿铺在桌上，逐行核对后又用笔尖划去其中一行名字。 One name was omitted from the final list.
sceneCN: 这里的 omitted 是「被删去、未被列入」（第 1 个义项：有意删去）；句意为最终名单上有一个名字被删掉了。图中可辨识物件：打印稿、笔尖、名单。

pos.zh: 省略；遗漏；不提及；排除在外

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 omittere 的词干 omiss- 加 -ion 构成，义为「省略；遗漏」
由 omiss- 加 -ible 构成，义为「可以省略的」
由 omiss- 加 -ive 构成，义为「省略的；遗漏的」

senses.title: Leaving something out on purpose
senses.definition: to leave out a word, detail or step deliberately, so that it is not included
senses.definitionCN: 有意不把某个词、细节或步骤放进去，使其不被包含在内
senses.example: The editor omitted the last paragraph to save space.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删去了最后一段以节省篇幅。
senses.why: Latin omittere meant to let go or let pass, so leaving something out is pictured as releasing it rather than destroying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 omittere 意为放走、让过去，所以「省去」被想成把东西放开，而不是把它毁掉。

senses.title: Leaving something out by mistake
senses.definition: to fail to include or do something because one forgot or overlooked it
senses.definitionCN: 因为忘记或看漏而没有把某事列入或没有去做
senses.example: Two names were omitted from the guest list by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 有两个名字被无意中漏在了宾客名单之外。
senses.why: The same act of letting something pass can happen with or without intent, and English keeps one verb for both the planned and the accidental gap.
senses.whyCN: 同样一个「让它过去」的动作，可能有意也可能无意，英语用同一个动词兼指计划中的空缺和疏忽造成的空缺。

senses.title: Saying nothing about something
senses.definition: to say nothing about something, whether from carelessness or from a wish to avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 对某事一字不提，不论是出于疏忽还是有意回避
senses.example: He omitted any mention of the delay in his report.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报告里对延误只字未提。
senses.why: If a word can be left out of a text, it can also be left out of speech, so the verb comes to mean passing over a matter in silence.
senses.whyCN: 一个词能从文本里省掉，也能从话语里省掉，于是这个动词就表示对一件事沉默地略过。

senses.title: Keeping someone off a list or group
senses.definition: to leave a person or thing out of a set, list or team, often as a decision
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物排除在一套名单或队伍之外，常是经过决定的
senses.example: The coach omitted him from the squad for the final.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把他排除在决赛的队员名单之外。
senses.why: A list is a set of chosen items, and whatever is not chosen is let go, so omission becomes a quiet way of excluding.
senses.whyCN: 名单是一组被选中项，凡没被选中的就被放开，于是「省去」也成了一种安静的排除方式。

intro.en: Omit comes from Latin omittere, a verb built from a prefix meaning away and mittere, to send or let go; the idea of releasing something explains why the word covers both deliberate cuts and accidental gaps.
intro.cn: omit 来自拉丁语 omittere，由表示「离开」的前缀与 mittere（送出、放走）构成；「把东西放开」这个想法解释了它为何兼指有意删削与无意遗漏。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the moving force inside a large family of English verbs.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，为英语一大族动词提供了内在的「送出」力量。

items.en: Ob- plus mittere, worn down to om-, gave omittere, to let go or let pass by, and its participle stem was omiss-.
items.cn: ob- 与 mittere 合成并磨变为 om-，得到 omittere，意为放走、让过去，其分词词干为 omiss-。

items.en: Old French took the verb as ometre, meaning to leave out or to fail to do, and used it of words and duties alike.
items.cn: 古法语借作 ometre，意为略去、漏做，词与职责都能接。

items.en: Middle English adopted it as omitten, and the modern spelling omit replaced the older ending in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语作 omitten，到十六世纪现代拼写 omit 取代了旧词尾。

items.en: Modern English keeps omit for leaving out words, facts, steps and people, and doubles the t in omitted and omitting because the stress falls on the last syllable.
items.cn: 现代英语让 omit 承担略去词语、事实、步骤与人，并因重音落在末音节而在 omitted、omitting 中双写 t。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb mittere, which is about sending; the near-meaning group collects verbs for leaving things or people out.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 mittere（送出）上的词；近义组收表示把事物或人排除在外的动词。

entries.definition: The act or result of leaving something out.
entries.definitionCN: 省去、遗漏的行为或结果。

entries.definition: To send out light, sound, heat or gas.
To send something in for consideration, or to yield.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物呈交上去供考虑，或表示屈服。

entries.definition: To allow something to happen or to give official consent.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事发生，或给予正式许可。

entries.definition: To pass over something and go on to the next one.
entries.definitionCN: 跳过某物，直接进入下一个。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something out of a group or place.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物排除在群体或场所之外。

entries.definition: To fail to give proper attention or care to something.
entries.definitionCN: 没有给予某事应有的注意或照料。

entries.definition: To leave something out, often from a plan, list or text.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从计划、名单或文本中去掉。

normalIntro.en: Omit hides a Latin verb of sending under a prefix meaning away, so every hook pictures something being let go rather than deleted.
normalIntro.cn: omit 在表示「离开」的前缀下藏着一个拉丁语「送出」动词，所以每条记忆钩子都想着某物被放开，而不是被删除。

normal.en: The visible part of omit is the Latin verb mittere, to send, and the prefix om- marks the movement away.
normal.cn: omit 看得见的部分是拉丁动词 mittere（送出），前缀 om- 标出「离开」的方向。

normal.en: Omitted and omitting double the t because the stress sits on the final syllable, as in admitted and permitting.
normal.cn: omitted 与 omitting 双写 t，因为重音落在最后一个音节，就像 admitted 与 permitting 一样。

normal.en: Omission is built on the participle stem omiss- plus -ion, the noun suffix for an act or its result.
normal.cn: omission 建立在分词词干 omiss- 上，加 -ion 这个表示行为或结果的名词后缀。

normal.en: Emit, submit and permit share the same mittere, so the family is about sending, not about leaving out.
normal.cn: emit、submit、permit 共用同一个 mittere，可见这一族词讲的是送出，而不是省去。

normal.en: Omit to mention is a fixed pattern meaning to forget to say, and it keeps the old sense of letting a duty pass.
normal.cn: omit to mention 是固定说法，意为忘记说，它保留了「让一项职责溜过去」的旧意思。

abstract.en: A gap can be a decision or an accident, and English lets one word hold both without apology.
abstract.cn: 一个空缺可以出于决定，也可以出于意外，而英语让同一个词把两者都装下，不作区分。

abstract.en: To omit is to trust that the missing piece will be noticed only when it matters.
abstract.cn: 省去，就是相信缺失的那一块只有在要紧时才会被人察觉。

abstract.en: The same verb that removes a word also removes a person, which shows how thin the line is between editing and exclusion.
abstract.cn: 删掉一个词的动词也能排除一个人，这说明编辑与排斥之间的界线多么细。

examples.en: The editor omitted the last paragraph to save space.
examples.cn: 编辑删去了最后一段以节省篇幅。

examples.en: Two names were omitted from the guest list by accident.
examples.cn: 两个名字被无意中漏在了宾客名单之外。

examples.en: He omitted any mention of the delay in his report.
examples.cn: 他在报告里对延误只字未提。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦米特」——米特把一行字悄悄放走，就漏了；记住 omit 是省略、遗漏。

root: 来自拉丁语 omittere（放走、让过去），由 ob-（离开、放下）与 mittere（送出）合成；分词词干 omiss- 构成 omission 等派生词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is letting something go; the senses divide by intention and by target, covering a planned cut, an accidental gap, a silence and an exclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把某物放开；义项按意图与对象分出有意删削、无意遗漏、沉默不提与排除在外。

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound: a prefix of departure plus the verb mittere, and its participle stem feeds the English nouns and adjectives built on omiss-.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语复合词：一个表示离开的前缀加动词 mittere，其分词词干又养育了以 omiss- 为基础的英语名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere, omittere and omissio are recorded, so the English family has a reliable Latin ancestry and a clear picture of sending away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere、omittere、omissio 均有记录，因此这一族英语词有可靠的拉丁语世系，也有清晰的「送走」画面。

definition_zh: 后部；后面的；抚养；饲养；抬起
definition_en: the back part of something; at or toward the back; to bring up a child; to breed animals; to raise something, especially the head
core_image: 马车后轮与车厢尾部
scene: 马车停在院门口，车尾对着台阶，后轮还沾着泥。 He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
sceneCN: 这里 rear 是「后部」（第 1 个义项：某物的后面部分）；句意为马车停在院门口，他转身朝房子后部走去。画面里可留意：马车尾部、后轮上的泥、台阶。

derivatives.zh: rear 加 -ward，指朝后的
rear 加 -most，指最后面的

senses.title: The back part
senses.definition: the back part of a building, vehicle or object
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、车辆或物体的后面部分
senses.example: He turned and walked toward the rear of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他转身朝房子后部走去。
senses.why: The back sense came from Old French riere and Latin retro, both meaning behind, and it names the part that lies at the back.
senses.whyCN: 「后面」之义来自古法语 riere 与拉丁语 retro，二者都意为「在后」，它命名位于后方的部分。

senses.title: At the back
senses.definition: located at or toward the back
senses.definitionCN: 位于后方或朝后的
senses.example: The rear window was steamed up with rain.
senses.exampleCN: 后窗被雨水蒙上了水汽。
senses.why: The adjective simply applies the back sense to a noun, marking the part that sits behind the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把「后面」的意思用于名词，标记位于其余部分之后的那一部分。

senses.title: To bring up a child
senses.definition: to care for a child until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子直到其长大
senses.example: She reared three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word, Old English ræran, to raise, and raising a child is lifting it toward adulthood.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词，即古英语 ræran（抬起），抚养孩子就是把他托向成年。

senses.title: To breed animals
senses.definition: to keep and breed animals or grow plants
senses.definitionCN: 饲养并繁殖动物，或栽培植物
senses.example: The farm rears sheep for wool.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养羊取毛。
senses.why: Animals are also raised up from young to grown, so the raising sense extends from children to livestock.
senses.whyCN: 动物也是从幼小被养到长成，于是「抬起」之义从孩子扩展到牲畜。

senses.title: To raise the head
senses.definition: to lift something, especially the head, often used of an animal or of something emerging
senses.definitionCN: 抬起某物，尤指头，常用于动物或某物冒现
senses.example: The horse reared its head at the sound.
senses.exampleCN: 马听到声音抬起了头。
senses.why: The oldest sense of ræran is to raise physically, and this literal lifting survives in phrases such as rear its head.
senses.whyCN: ræran 最古老的意思就是实际抬起，这种字面抬起保留在 rear its head 等说法中。

intro.en: Rear is really two words that came to share one spelling: the back sense from Old French riere and Latin retro, and the raising sense from Old English ræran.
intro.cn: rear 其实是两个词共用一个拼写：表示「后面」的义项来自古法语 riere 与拉丁语 retro，表示「抬起」的义项来自古英语 ræran。

items.en: Riere meant behind, and it named the back part of a place or a formation.
items.cn: riere 意为在后，命名一处地方或队列的后部。

items.en: Retro meant backward, and it stands behind the back sense of rear as well as words like retrograde.
items.cn: retro 意为向后，它支撑着 rear 的「后面」义以及与 retrograde 等词的关联。

items.en: Ræran meant to raise or bring up, and it is the source of the farming and family senses.
items.cn: ræran 意为抬起或养育，是饲养与抚养义项的来源。

items.en: The two words came to share the spelling rear, so one form now carries both the back and the raising.
items.cn: 两个词共用 rear 这一拼写，于是一个形式同时承载「后面」与「抬起」。

items.en: Modern English uses rear for the back, for what is behind, for bringing up children and animals, and for lifting the head.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rear 指后部、后面的、抚养孩子与饲养动物，以及抬起头。

definition_zh: 平行的；类似的；类似的事物；与……相似；与……同时发生
definition_en: of lines, always the same distance apart and never meeting; similar in important ways; a person or thing resembling another; to be similar to or to happen at the same time as
core_image: 两条铁轨并肩伸向远方，始终不碰在一起
scene: 两条铁轨穿过田野，一直伸到看不见的地方。 The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
sceneCN: 这里 parallel 是「平行的」（第 1 个义项：两条线距离处处相同、永不相交）；句意为这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。图中可辨识物件：铁轨、枕木、远处的隧道口。

pos.zh: 类似的事物；可类比的对象

由 parallel 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed 构成，指无可比拟的

senses.title: Always the same distance apart
senses.definition: of two or more lines or surfaces, keeping the same distance apart at every point so that they never meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条或多条线、面的距离处处相等，因而永不相交
senses.example: The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。
senses.why: Greek parallelos joins para, beside, with allelos, one another: two things set beside each other with an unbroken gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 parallelos 由 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此）拼成：两样东西彼此并排，中间隔着一道始终不变的距离。

senses.title: Similar in important ways
senses.definition: similar in a way that allows one thing to be compared with another, especially in structure or development
senses.definitionCN: 在结构或发展上相似到可以彼此对照
senses.example: The two cities followed parallel paths of growth after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后这两座城市走上了相似的发展道路。
senses.why: Lines that never meet still hold a constant relation, so the word came to name things that move in step without ever touching.
senses.whyCN: 永不相交的线仍保持固定的关系，于是这个词也用来指那些同步前进、却从不接触的事物。

senses.title: A person or thing like another
senses.titleCN: 类似的事物；可类比的对象
senses.definition: a person, event or situation that can be compared with another because of a clear resemblance
senses.definitionCN: 因为明显相像而可以拿来与另一者比较的人、事件或处境
senses.example: Historians drew a parallel between the two collapses.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这两次崩塌放在一起比较。
senses.why: Once the adjective names resemblance, the noun can name the second item itself, giving speakers a way to say that one thing is another's counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦表示相似，名词就能指那第二个对象本身，让人可以直说一件事是另一件事的对应物。

senses.title: To be similar to or happen alongside
senses.definition: to be similar to something, or to happen at the same time and in a connected way
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相似，或与它同时发生并彼此关联
senses.example: The rise in rents paralleled the growth of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨与这座城市的发展同步发生。
senses.why: The verb sets that picture in motion: two courses of events keep the same gap and move forward together.
senses.whyCN: 动词把那幅画面变成运动：两条事态的线索保持同样的间距，一起向前推进。

intro.en: Parallel comes from a Greek adjective meaning beside one another, built for geometry and later borrowed into Latin and English as a term of lines and likeness.
intro.cn: parallel 来自一个意为「彼此并排」的希腊形容词，本为几何学而造，后来被拉丁语与英语借用，用来指线与相似。

items.en: Parallelos joined para, beside, with allelos, one another, and described things set side by side at an even distance.
items.cn: parallelos 把 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此）拼在一起，描述以相等距离并排摆放的东西。

items.en: Greek geometers used the word for straight lines in one plane that never meet, and this technical sense has never been lost.
items.cn: 希腊几何学家用这个词指同一平面内永不相交的直线，这一专业义至今没有丢失。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as parallelus; it was a learned borrowing rather than a word inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 parallelus；这是学术借用，不是从拉丁语本土传下的词。

items.en: English took the word by way of Latin and French, first for geometry and soon after for any two things that resemble each other.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁语与法语借入这个词，先用于几何，随后很快用于任何彼此相像的两样东西。

items.en: Modern English keeps the geometrical sense, adds similarity and events running side by side, and uses the noun for a counterpart.
items.cn: 现代英语保留几何义，增加了相似与并行发生的意思，并用名词形式指对应物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other Greek compounds that begin with the same short element, each built on a different stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for likeness and for a matching thing.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以同一个短小成分开头的希腊复合词，每个词接的词干都不同；近义组收表示相似以及对应物的词。

entries.definition: Greek para plus graphein, to write; the prefix looks the same but the formation is separate, not a shared family.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 graphein（写）；前缀写法相同，但构词各自独立，不是同一词族。

entries.definition: Para beside plus doxa opinion, a claim that runs against common belief.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 doxa（意见），指违背常见看法的说法。

entries.definition: Para beside plus sitos food, one who eats at another person's table.
entries.definitionCN: para（在旁边）加 sitos（食物），指在别人桌边吃饭的寄生者。

entries.definition: Greek para plus allassein, to change; it shares the all- element with parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 para 加 allassein（改变）；与 parallel 共享 all- 这一成分。

entries.definition: Almost the same, but not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎相同，但并不完全一样。

entries.definition: Similar in a way that allows a comparison between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 相似到可以把两者放在一起比较。

entries.definition: A person or thing that has the same role as another elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处担任同一角色的人或事物。

entries.definition: Next to and parallel with something.

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek picture of two things laid side by side, and the whole family keeps the ideas of even distance, likeness and a matching partner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语里两样东西并排放置的画面，整族词都带着等距、相似与配对这三层意思。

normal.en: The Greek parts are para, beside, and allelos, one another, so parallel lines are lines placed beside each other.
normal.cn: 希腊部件是 para（在旁边）与 allelos（彼此），所以平行线就是彼此并排放着的线。

normal.en: The same picture yields the sense of similar: two courses stay side by side without ever meeting.
normal.cn: 同一幅画面也生出「相似」：两条走向并排前进，却始终不相交。

normal.en: Parallel ends in -el with one r, while parallelism adds -ism and keeps the same l-sound.
normal.cn: parallel 以一个 r、结尾 -el 拼写，parallelism 则加 -ism，l 音不变。

normal.en: In parallel means two things are running at the same time, like two tracks carrying trains.
normal.cn: in parallel 指两件事同时进行，就像两条各跑列车的轨道。

normal.en: The verb is regular: parallels, paralleled, paralleling, with the final l doubled.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：parallels、paralleled、paralleling，末尾的 l 双写。

abstract.en: Parallel lines are a promise that two things can stay close forever without ever becoming one.
abstract.cn: 平行线是一种承诺：两样东西可以永远靠得很近，却始终不合成一个。

abstract.en: To draw a parallel is to say that two separate stories are running on the same track.
abstract.cn: 把两者作类比，就是说两个互不相干的故事跑在同一条轨道上。

abstract.en: A parallel universe is the everyday metaphor for a life that kept the same distance from this one.
abstract.cn: 平行宇宙是日常语言里对「另一种人生」的比喻：它与这一种人生始终隔着同样的距离。

examples.en: The two railway lines run parallel for miles before the tunnel.
examples.cn: 这两条铁轨并行数英里，之后才进入隧道。

examples.en: The two cities followed parallel paths of growth after the war.
examples.cn: 战后这两座城市走上了相似的发展道路。

examples.en: The rise in rents paralleled the growth of the city.
examples.cn: 租金的上涨与这座城市的发展同步发生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「排啊排」——两条线一直排着走，谁也不碰谁；记住 parallel 是平行。

root: 希腊语 para（在旁边）加 allelos（彼此）构成 parallelos，指彼此并排、距离相等的线；经中世纪拉丁语 parallelus 与法语进入英语。它与 paragraph 虽然同写 para-，但接的词干不同，是两套独立的构词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things laid side by side at a fixed distance; the senses move from geometry to resemblance, to a matching partner, and to events that run alongside each other.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是以固定距离并排放置的两样东西；义项从几何走到相似，再到对应物，最后是并行发生的事件。

branches.en: rents and population climbing together on a chart

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound of a preposition and a pronoun meaning one another, and English suffixes then build the nouns and adjectives around it.

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; medieval Latin parallelus is a learned borrowing of the Greek adjective, so the Latin form follows the Greek rather than feeding it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；中世纪拉丁语的 parallelus 是对希腊形容词的学术借用，拉丁形式是跟着希腊语走的，而非其来源。

senses.title: Side taken

definition_zh: 在船（车、飞机）上；上船（车、飞机）
definition_en: on or onto a ship, train, aircraft or other vehicle
core_image: 一个人踏上舷梯，手扶着栏杆
scene: 码头上，旅客提着箱子依次走上舷梯。 The passengers were already aboard when the whistle blew.
sceneCN: 这里的 aboard 指「在船上」（第 1 个义项：处于船、车或飞机之上）；句意是汽笛响时乘客已经在船上了。

derivatives.zh: 义为「随车携带的；入职的」
义为「登乘；寄宿」

senses.title: On a ship
senses.definition: in or on a ship
senses.definitionCN: 在船体之内或船板之上
senses.example: The passengers were already aboard when the whistle blew.
senses.exampleCN: 汽笛响时乘客已经在船上了。
senses.why: The oldest phrase was on bord, upon the ship's deck, and aboard still means that.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的说法是 on bord，即「在船板上」，aboard 至今仍是这个意思。

senses.title: Onto a ship
senses.definition: moving onto a ship
senses.definitionCN: 移动到船上
senses.example: The last guests came aboard at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一批客人在中午上了船。
senses.why: The same word covers position and movement, as many place words do.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词兼指位置与移动，许多方位词都是如此。

senses.title: On a train or plane
senses.definition: in or on a train, bus or aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 在火车、公共汽车或飞机上
senses.example: No smoking is allowed aboard the aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机上禁止吸烟。
senses.why: Once ships named the pattern, every large vehicle inherited the word.
senses.whyCN: 船先立下了这个说法，各种大型交通工具便都继承了它。

senses.title: The call to board
senses.definition: in all aboard, the shout that departure is near
senses.definitionCN: 在 all aboard 中，提示即将出发的呼号
senses.example: The guard shouted all aboard just before the doors closed.
senses.exampleCN: 车门关闭前，列车员喊了一声「全部上车」。
senses.why: A call to be on board became a fixed announcement, and the word kept it.
senses.whyCN: 叫大家上船的话成了固定广播，这个词便保留下来。

senses.title: Welcome to a group
senses.definition: in welcome aboard, an invitation to join a team
senses.definitionCN: 在 welcome aboard 中，表示欢迎加入一个团队
senses.example: The captain welcomed the new engineer aboard.
senses.exampleCN: 船长欢迎新工程师加入。
senses.why: A crew is a company on a ship, so joining any team borrows the nautical welcome.
senses.whyCN: 船员是船上的一群人，加入任何团队都借用了这句航海欢迎。

senses.title: Near a ship
senses.definition: in close aboard, lying near a vessel's side
senses.definitionCN: 在 close aboard 中，指靠近船侧
senses.example: The pilot boat stood close aboard.
senses.exampleCN: 引航艇紧靠着大船。
senses.why: Being at the side of a ship is a specialised extension of being on it.
senses.whyCN: 处在船侧是「在船上」的一个专门延伸。

senses.title: On a spacecraft
senses.definition: in or on a spacecraft or space station
senses.definitionCN: 在航天器或空间站上
senses.example: The crew slept aboard the station for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 机组在空间站上睡了六个月。
senses.why: Spacecraft are ships in name and in practice, so the word travels with them.
senses.whyCN: 航天器在名称与实操上都像船，这个词便随之前往。

senses.title: To take something in
senses.definition: in take aboard, to load cargo or accept an idea
senses.definitionCN: 在 take aboard 中，指装载货物或接受某种想法
senses.example: The team took the new idea aboard after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间讨论，团队采纳了这个新想法。
senses.why: Loading a ship and accepting an idea are both taking something on board.
senses.whyCN: 往船上装货与接受一个想法，都是「把东西接到船上」。

senses.why: Old English middæg is literally mid plus day, so the word began as a label for the point that splits the day in two; noon is exactly that point.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 middæg 字面就是 mid 加 day，这个词最初只是给「把一天切成两半」的那个位置贴标签；正午恰恰就是那个位置。

senses.title: The hours around noon
senses.definition: the period on either side of noon, when people eat and rest
senses.definitionCN: 正午前后的一段时间，人们在这时吃饭、歇息
senses.example: The square stays busy through midday.
senses.exampleCN: 广场在整个中午时段都很热闹。
senses.why: Once the word names the peak of the day, it easily widens to the hours that surround the peak, because meals and rests cluster around that moment.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指到一天的最高点，就很容易扩展到围绕这个点的那几个小时，因为吃饭与休息都集中在那个时段。

senses.title: The strongest light and heat of the day
senses.definition: the bright, hot quality of the day at its height
senses.definitionCN: 一天走到最高处时那种明亮、炎热的特质
senses.example: The cactus folds its flowers against the midday sun.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人掌把花收拢起来，以避开正午的烈日。
senses.why: Because the sun stands highest then, midday also names the glare and heat of that moment; the word shifts from a clock reading to a felt condition.
senses.whyCN: 因为太阳此时最高，midday 也指那一刻的强光与炎热；词义便从钟点读数转到身体感受到的状态。

senses.title: Happening at noon
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that takes place or appears at noon
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指在正午发生或出现的事物
senses.example: They packed a midday meal for the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为长途步行准备了一顿午餐。
senses.why: English lets a time noun sit before another noun like an adjective; midday meal and midday break simply compress at midday into a single word, with no change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许时间名词像形容词一样放在另一个名词前；midday meal 与 midday break 只是把 at midday 压缩成一个词，形式并没有变化。

intro.en: Midday is an ancient compound: the root for middle was joined to the word for day before English existed as a separate language.
intro.cn: midday 是一个古老的复合词：在英语尚未成为独立语言之前，表示「中间」的词根就已经和表示「日」的词连在一起了。

items.en: The compound *midjadagaz joined the root for middle to the word for day, so the middle of the day was named as one unit.
items.cn: *midjadagaz 把表示「中间」的词根与表示「日」的词连成一个单位，一天的正中由此有了专门的名字。

items.en: Old English middæg carried the compound into daily use alongside midd, and it named the point where morning and afternoon meet.
items.cn: 古英语的 middæg 与 midd 一起进入日常使用，用来指上午与下午交会的那一点。

items.en: Middle English kept midday as the name of the noon hour and began to place it before other nouns, as in midday meal.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 midday 指正午时刻，并开始把它放在其他名词前面，如 midday meal。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries extended midday to the surrounding hours and to the heat and glare of noon.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者把 midday 扩展到正午前后的几个小时，也用来指正午的炎热与强光。

items.en: Modern English uses midday for noon, for the hours around it, and attributively in compounds such as midday sun and midday break.
items.cn: 现代英语用 midday 指正午、指正午前后，也作定语用于 midday sun、midday break 之类的复合说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds made with the same mid prefix; the near-meaning group collects other names for noon and the lunch hour.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 mid 前缀构成的复合词；近义组收其他表示正午与午饭时段的说法。

entries.definition: The middle of the week.
The middle part of the morning.
The middle part of the afternoon.
The middle of the day; this word is built on noon rather than on mid, so it is only close in spelling and meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 一天的正中；这个词由 noon 而非 mid 构成，只是拼写与含义相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Twelve o'clock in the day.
The period around noon.

normalIntro.en: Midday is a transparent compound of mid and day, and the words around it keep the same recipe of middle plus a unit of time.
normalIntro.cn: midday 是 mid 与 day 组成的透明复合词，它周围的说法也都沿用了「中间加时间单位」的配方。

normal.en: Midday is mid plus day, so the word is a small picture of a day cut in half.
normal.cn: midday 就是 mid 加 day，这个词本身就是「把一天切成两半」的小画面。

normal.en: The main stress falls on the second half, mid-DAY, which is why it sounds like one point rather than two separate words.
normal.cn: 主重音落在后半段 mid-DAY 上，所以它听起来像一个时间点，而不是两个独立的词。

normal.en: Latin meridies, from medius and dies, follows the same recipe: middle plus day.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 meridies 由 medius 与 dies 合成，走的是同一条思路：中间加日。

normal.en: Midday meal and midday sun show the noun acting like an adjective without any added ending.
normal.cn: midday meal 与 midday sun 展示了这个名词不靠任何词尾就充当形容词。

normal.en: Set it beside midnight: the same middle, but on the other side of the clock.
normal.cn: 把它和 midnight 放在一起看：同样是「中间」，只是落在钟面的另一侧。

abstract.en: A shadow shrinking to the feet is the body's own clock announcing midday.
abstract.cn: 影子缩到脚边，就是身体自带的钟在宣告正午。

abstract.en: Midday is the hinge of the day: morning on one side, afternoon on the other.
abstract.cn: midday 是一天的铰链：一边是上午，一边是下午。

abstract.en: Two ideas, middle and day, are stored inside one short sound.
abstract.cn: 「中间」与「日」两个概念，被收进了一个短短的声音里。

examples.en: The bells rang at midday.
examples.cn: 正午时分钟声响起。

examples.en: We spent the whole midday walking through the old town.
examples.cn: 我们整个中午都在老城里走。

examples.en: The cactus folds its flowers against the midday sun.
examples.cn: 仙人掌把花收拢起来，以避开正午的烈日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密的」加「得」——太阳密得头顶发烫，一天正好走到正中；midday 是正午。

root: 古英语 middæg，由 midd（中间）与 dæg（日、天）复合；拉丁语 meridies（medius 中间 + dies 日）用的是同一种构词思路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the peak of the day; the senses spread out from that point to the noon hour, the hours around it, the heat of the moment, and attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一天的最高点；各义项从这个点扩到正午时刻、前后时段、当时的炎热，以及作定语的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sun directly overhead and a shadow shrunk to the feet.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳正悬在头顶，影子缩到脚边。

branches.en: bells striking as the shadow vanishes
branches.cn: 影子缩到脚边时响起的钟声

branches.en: stalls closing while people rest
branches.cn: 人们歇息、摊子收起的时刻

branches.en: a cactus closing its flowers against the glare
branches.cn: 仙人掌在强光里收拢花朵

branches.en: a packed meal waiting for a long walk
branches.cn: 为长途步行备好的饭盒

branches.en: a market square emptied by heat
branches.cn: 被炎热赶空的集市广场

intro.en: Midday is held together by a middle root and a day noun, and Latin built its own word for noon from exactly the same two ideas.
intro.cn: midday 由表示「中间」的词根和表示「日」的名词合成，拉丁语用完全相同的两个概念造出了自己的「正午」。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 直径；直径长度；口径
definition_en: a straight line across a circle through its centre, or the length of that line
core_image: 一根细线从圆的一边穿过圆心拉到另一边
scene: 木匠把圆桌翻过来，用卷尺从一边量到另一边，尺子正好过中心。 The diameter of the table is one metre.
sceneCN: 这里 diameter 指「直径」（第 1 个义项：穿过圆心、两端落在圆上的线段）；句意是这张桌子的直径是一米。

derivatives.zh: 直径的；截然相反的
完全地；正好相反地
直径的

senses.title: A line across a circle
senses.definition: a straight line that passes through the centre of a circle and touches both sides
senses.definitionCN: 穿过圆心、两端都落在圆上的直线
senses.example: The diameter of the table is one metre.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子的直径是一米。
senses.why: The longest straight path through a round thing must pass its centre.
senses.whyCN: 穿过一个圆东西的最长直线，必然经过它的中心。

senses.title: The length measured that way
senses.definition: the length of such a line, used as a measure of how wide a round thing is
senses.definitionCN: 这条线的长度，用来衡量圆形物体有多宽
senses.example: The circle has a diameter of ten centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个圆的直径是十厘米。
senses.why: One number can stand for the whole width of a circle.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字，就能代表一个圆整个的宽度。

senses.title: The width of a round opening
senses.definition: the width of a tube, pipe or opening measured across its centre
senses.definitionCN: 管子、管道或开口穿过中心量出的宽度
senses.example: The pipe has an internal diameter of ten centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 这根管子的内径是十厘米。
senses.why: A pipe is only a circle pulled out into length.
senses.whyCN: 一根管子，不过是把圆拉成了长度。

intro.en: Diameter comes from Greek diametros, a measuring across, built from dia-, across, and metron, a measure.
intro.cn: diameter 来自希腊语 diametros（横量过去），由 dia-（横穿）与 metron（量度）构成。

items.en: Metron meant a measure or a unit of length.
items.cn: metron 指量度或长度单位。

items.en: Diametros meant the measure taken straight across a circle.
items.cn: diametros 指横穿一个圆量出的长度。

items.en: Latin diametrus brought the word into geometry books.
items.cn: 拉丁语 diametrus 把这个词带进了几何书。

items.en: English diameter named the line through the centre.
items.cn: 英语 diameter 指穿过中心的那条线。

items.en: It now also measures pipes, lenses and other round openings.
items.cn: 如今它也用来量管子、镜片以及其他圆形开口。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dia- opening, while the meaning group names other measurements of width.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dia- 开头，近义组则指其他几种宽度的量度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diameter 记成「带个米特」：dia 是横穿，meter 是量，横着穿过圆心量一量，就是直径。

root: 来自希腊语 diametros，由 dia-（横穿）与 metron（量度）组成，本义是横穿圆量出的长度。经拉丁语进入几何学，后来除表示穿过圆心的线段与长度外，也用于表示管子、镜片等圆形开口的口径。

sensesIntro.en: From the longest line in a circle, to the number that reports it, to the inside width of a pipe.
sensesIntro.cn: 从圆里最长的那条线，到报出这个长度的数字，再到一根管子的内宽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine line crossing a circle exactly through its centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细线正好穿过圆心横跨一个圆。

branches.en: The first sense is the line itself, drawn through the middle.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那条穿过中间的线本身。

branches.en: The second sense is the number that line gives.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是那条线给出的数字。

branches.en: The third sense is the same number read inside a tube.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同一个数字在管子里被读出来。

branches.en: A line and a length are one fact told two ways.

branches.en: A tabletop and a pipe are both measured across their middle.
branches.cn: 桌面与管子，都是穿过中间去量。

latinIntro.cn: 词基 metron 意为量度，前缀 dia- 说明这次量是横穿过去的。
