definition_zh: 自由；自由权；擅自；获准行动的范围
definition_en: freedom to live and act as one chooses, especially as a condition protected by law or constitution
core_image: 一根被砸断的锁链落在石阶上，锁孔里还插着半截钥匙，人已经走远
scene: 城邦的公民在广场上宣读宪章，声称任何人不得未经审判而被拘押。 Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
sceneCN: 这里指「受法律保障、不受任意拘押的个人自由」，对应第 1 个义项：法律保护的、免于任意逮捕的自由；句意为公民宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人。画面要点：广场、宪章、砸断的锁链。

pos.zh: 自由；自由权（不可数；表示各项具体自由时可用复数）

collocations.zh: 获准的；自由的；有空闲的

derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽容的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的、宽厚的」形容词经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

senses.title: Protection from arbitrary detention
senses.titleCN: 免于任意拘押的个人自由
senses.definition: the condition of a person who cannot be arrested or held except by lawful procedure
senses.definitionCN: 除依法定程序外不得被逮捕或拘押的个人状态
senses.example: Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 公民在广场宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人，这是对个人自由的保障。
senses.why: In Roman law the free person's body could not be seized at will, so liberty begins as a legal status rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法中，自由人的身体不能被随意捉拿，因此「自由」一开始是一种法律身份，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Self-government of a community
senses.definition: the condition of a city or people that makes its own laws instead of receiving them from a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 城市或民族自行立法、而不是从统治者那里接受法律的状态
senses.example: The city kept its liberties against the duke for two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城邦两代人以来一直保有对抗公爵的自由权。
senses.why: Medieval towns bought charters that listed their liberties, so the word came to name a body's collective self-rule.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪城镇买下特许状，状上逐条列出它们的自由权，于是这个词也命名一个群体的自治。

senses.title: Specific rights protected by law
senses.titleCN: 法律保护的各项具体自由权
senses.definition: the several freedoms, such as speech, worship and assembly, that a constitution or statute guarantees
senses.definitionCN: 宪法或法律所保障的若干项自由，如言论、礼拜与集会
senses.example: The bill lists the liberties that the state may not remove.
senses.exampleCN: 权利法案列出了国家不得取消的各项自由。
senses.why: The abstract condition becomes countable when each guarantee is written down separately, which is why the plural is so common in legal texts.
senses.whyCN: 当每一项保障被分别写下来，抽象状态就变得可数，这就是复数形式在法律文本中如此常见的原因。

senses.title: Overstepping what is allowed
senses.definition: the act of acting beyond one's permitted scope, especially in a way that is presumptuous
senses.definitionCN: 超出自己被允许的范围行事，尤指冒失无礼地这样做
senses.example: The visitor took liberties with the archive and rearranged the files.
senses.exampleCN: 那位访客擅自摆弄档案，把文件重新排列了。
senses.why: A granted latitude can be used too far, so the same noun turns ironic and names the abuse of a permission.
senses.whyCN: 获准的余地可能被用过了头，于是同一个名词转为反讽，命名对许可的滥用。

senses.title: Being permitted or free to act
senses.definition: the state of being allowed to do something, or of being free from obligation at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 获准做某事、或在某一时刻没有义务在身的状态
senses.example: You are at liberty to inspect the records yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以自行查阅这些记录。
senses.why: The phrase 'at liberty' keeps the old legal sense of a person not under restraint, and from it comes the polite formula for permission.
senses.whyCN: 「处于自由状态」这一短语保留了「人未受拘束」的旧法律义，礼貌的许可说法正是从这里来的。

senses.title: Freedom of conscience and worship
senses.definition: the right to hold and practise a faith without state pressure
senses.definitionCN: 不受国家压力地持有并实践信仰的权利
senses.example: Religious liberty was the first liberty to be argued for in print.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教自由是最早被以印刷文字论证的自由。
senses.why: Where the state and the church were the same body, the demand to worship otherwise was the sharpest test of a protected sphere.
senses.whyCN: 当国家与教会合为一体，要求以别的方式礼拜，就成了对「受保护领域」最尖锐的检验。

senses.title: Freedom of the will
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that a person can choose without being wholly determined by prior causes
senses.definitionCN: 人能够作出选择、而不完全被先在原因所决定的哲学主张
senses.example: The essay asks whether liberty of the will survives a strict causal account.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章追问，在严格的决定论解释下，意志自由是否还能成立。
senses.why: Once legal restraint is removed, the remaining question is whether anything else restrains the will, and the word follows the question inward.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律约束被移除，剩下的问题就是是否有别的东西在约束意志，这个词便随问题向内走。

senses.title: The range of a granted freedom
senses.definition: the extent of a place or body of knowledge that a person is allowed to use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人被允许使用的场所或知识范围
senses.example: The scholar was given the liberty of the whole collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者获准自由使用全部藏书。
senses.why: To have the liberty of a place is an old civic formula: not ownership, but the permitted run of it.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有某地的自由」是一个古老的市民说法：不是所有权，而是被允许在其中往来。

intro.en: Liberty comes from Latin libertas, the condition of a free person, built on liber 'free'. The deeper origin of liber is uncertain. English took the word through Old French, and its plural came to mean specific chartered privileges.
intro.cn: liberty 出自拉丁语 libertas，指自由人的身份，建立在 liber「自由的」之上。liber 的更深来源不确定。英语经古法语吸收此词，其复数后来指特许状上具体列明的特权。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, not a slave' and could also describe a person of noble or generous status. Its own origin is uncertain; a connection with a root meaning 'to grow' has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、非奴隶的」，也可形容出身高贵或气度宽厚的人。它本身的来源不确定；有人提出它与意为「生长」的词根相关，但未获确立。

items.en: Libertas named the condition of a free person and, in Roman public life, the status that law protected against arbitrary seizure.
items.cn: libertas 指自由人的身份；在罗马公共生活中，它指法律保护、免于任意捉拿的身份。

items.en: Old French liberte carried the noun into English, at first in religious and civic contexts rather than in philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语 liberte 把这个名词带入英语，最初用于宗教与市民语境，而不是哲学。

items.en: Towns and guilds listed their liberties in charters, and the plural became a name for specific privileges held by a body.
items.cn: 城镇与行会在特许状中逐条列出自己的自由权，其复数形式于是成为某个群体所持具体特权的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the singular named a general political condition, and documents began to speak of civil liberty. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，单数形式指一般的政治状态，文书开始谈论公民自由。年代为约数。

items.en: The same noun was applied to the will, producing the long debate over liberty of the will that continues in philosophy.
items.cn: 同一个名词被用到意志上，产生了关于意志自由的长期争论，这一争论在哲学中延续至今。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective or looks deceptively close to it, including one word whose Latin source is a different noun altogether; the second group gives near alternatives.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个拉丁形容词构成或与它形近得容易误认，其中还有一个词的拉丁来源是另一个名词；第二组是近义替代。

entries.definition: Generous or open-minded, and in politics favourable to reform; it began as 'of a free person' and moved toward generosity of attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 宽厚的、开明的，政治上倾向改革；它起初意为「自由人的」，后来转向态度上的宽宏。

entries.definition: To set a person or place free from control; it names the act that produces liberty rather than the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或地方脱离控制；它命名产生自由的动作，而不是状态。

entries.definition: A place where books are kept; its Latin source is a word for a book or the bark used for writing, not the adjective for freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书之所；它的拉丁来源是表示「书」或书写用树皮的词，而不是表示自由的形容词。

entries.definition: A published false statement that harms a reputation; it comes from a small Latin book or booklet, with no link to freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表的、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与自由无关。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being bound; it covers body, will and speech, while liberty more often names a legally protected status.
entries.definitionCN: 不受束缚的一般状态；它覆盖身体、意志与言论，而本词更常指受法律保护的身份。

entries.definition: The right of a person or region to govern itself; it stresses who makes the rules rather than what is forbidden.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或地区自行治理的权利；它强调由谁制定规则，而不是禁止什么。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another; it is common for nations and for self-supporting people.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态；常用于国家与自食其力的人。

entries.definition: An official permission to do something; it is narrower than liberty because it is granted case by case and can be revoked.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方许可；它比自由窄，因为逐案授予且可被撤回。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for a free person, real derived words and real legal formulas, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示自由人的形容词、真实派生词与真实法律套语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is a legal status: a free body that cannot be seized at will.
normal.cn: 核心是一种法律身份：一具不能被随意捉拿的自由身体。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberate, liberation and libertarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括宽厚的、解放、解放过程与自由意志论者。

normal.en: Medieval towns kept their liberties in written charters, which is why the plural means specific privileges.
normal.cn: 中世纪城镇把自由权写进特许状，所以复数形式指具体特权。

normal.en: The phrase at liberty means both free from restraint and free to act.
normal.cn: 「处于自由状态」这一说法既指不受拘束，也指可以行动。

normal.en: Taking liberties is the ironic side: using a permission further than it was given.
normal.cn: 「擅自」是这个词的反讽一面：把许可用得比给予的更远。

abstract.en: Picture a broken chain on a step with the key still in the lock, and the person already out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上一根断链，钥匙还插在锁里，人已经走远。

abstract.en: Picture a charter rolled open on a town table, each paragraph a named freedom.
abstract.cn: 想象城镇桌上一卷摊开的特许状，每一段都是一项有名字的自由。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked permission that opens only when the right name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「许可」的门，只有说出正确的名分才会打开。

examples.en: The court held that the detention violated his liberty.
examples.cn: 法院认定这次拘押侵犯了他的自由。

examples.en: You are at liberty to leave whenever you wish.
examples.cn: 你随时都可以离开。

examples.en: The reporter took liberties with the quotation and changed its sense.
examples.cn: 那名记者擅自改动引文，改变了它的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离不体」——身体离开束缚，就不必再贴着锁链过日子；自由就是能走开的那一步。

root: 拉丁语 liber「自由的、非奴隶的」→ libertas「自由人的身份」→ 经古法语 liberte 进入英语。liber 的更深来源不确定，与意为「生长」的词根相关的说法属假说；同族的 liberalis 意为「自由人的、宽厚的」，是另一条语义支线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a free body that the law may not seize. From that status come self-rule for a community, the list of named guarantees, the permission formula, the ironic overstepping of permission, the freedom of worship, the philosophical liberty of the will, and the old civic right to move through a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一具法律不得随意捉拿的自由身体开始。从这个身份分出共同体的自治、逐条列名的保障、许可的说法、对许可的反讽式越界、信仰的自由、哲学上的意志自由，以及古老的、可在某地往来的市民权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain broken at the link, with the key still turning in the lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：链环被砸断的锁链，钥匙还在锁里转动。

branches.en: UNBOUND BODY: protection from arbitrary arrest, and the polite formula that a person is free to act.
branches.cn: 不受束缚的身体：免于任意逮捕，以及「可以自由行动」的礼貌说法。

branches.en: SELF-RULE: a town or people that makes its own law.
branches.cn: 自治：自行立法的城镇或民族。

branches.en: NAMED GUARANTEES: the several liberties written in a charter, and the permitted run of a place.
branches.cn: 列名的保障：写进特许状的各项自由，以及在某地获准走动的范围。

branches.en: OVERSTEPPING: the same permission used beyond what was granted.
branches.cn: 越界：同一份许可被用得超出所给予的范围。

branches.en: CONSCIENCE AND WILL: worship without pressure, and the inner question of whether the will is determined.
branches.cn: 良心与意志：不受压力的礼拜，以及意志是否被决定的内在问题。

intro.en: The whole family rests on one Latin adjective for a free person, with noun, verb and agent endings added over time; the Germanic near synonym freedom belongs to a separate history.
intro.cn: 整个家族都依托一个表示自由人的拉丁形容词，随后加上名词、动词与施事后缀；日耳曼语的近义词「自由」属于另一段历史。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the derived adjective for generosity of character.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及由它派生、表示气度宽厚的形容词。

items.meaning: the condition of a free person
items.example: The charter guaranteed the liberty of every citizen.
items.exampleCN: 宪章保障每位公民的自由。

items.meaning: of a free person; generous, open-minded
items.meaningCN: 自由人的；宽厚的、开明的
items.example: A liberal education once meant the studies fit for a free person.
items.exampleCN: 「自由教育」原指适合自由人研习的科目。

items.meaningCN: 宽厚，尤指态度上的宽容
items.example: The host was praised for his liberality.
items.exampleCN: 主人因宽厚而受到称赞。

items.example: The troops liberated the occupied town.
items.exampleCN: 部队解放了被占领的城镇。

items.example: The museum marks the anniversary of the liberation.
The general was hailed as a liberator.
items.exampleCN: 那位将军被称颂为解放者。

items.meaning: one who holds personal freedom to be the highest value
items.meaningCN: 主张个人自由至上的人
items.example: The candidate described himself as a libertarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位候选人自称自由意志论者。

items.example: The measure was criticised as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The villagers gave thanks for their deliverance.

latinEntries.meaning: freedom; the status of a free person

derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽厚的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的」形容词加形容词后缀，经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

definition_zh: 邮费；邮资；邮票等邮资凭证；邮资标准
definition_en: the charge paid for sending a letter or parcel, or the stamps and marks that pay it
core_image: 一封贴好邮票的信，右上角盖着一枚邮戳
scene: 她把信封放到柜台的秤上，店员看了一眼重量，报出一个数目。 The clerk weighed the parcel and told her how much postage it needed.
sceneCN: 这里是「邮费」（第 1 个义项：寄件要付的钱）；句意为店员称了包裹，告诉她需要付多少邮费。画面里可留意那台秤、信封和邮票。

derivatives.zh: 由 post 加 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」
postage 去掉后缀 -age 得到的词根，指邮政
postage 与 stamp 复合，指用来支付邮资的邮票

senses.title: The charge for sending mail
senses.definition: the amount of money you must pay to send a letter or parcel by post
senses.definitionCN: 通过邮政寄送信件或包裹时必须支付的金额
senses.example: Postage to Europe has gone up again.
senses.exampleCN: 寄往欧洲的邮费又涨了。
senses.why: The suffix -age turns post into the cost attached to posting, the same way it names a fee in other words.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -age 把 post 变成「邮寄所附带的费用」，与其他词中用 -age 表示费用的做法一致。

senses.title: Stamps or printed marks that pay the charge
senses.definition: the stamps or printed marks stuck on mail to show that the charge has been paid
senses.definitionCN: 贴在邮件上、表示费用已付的邮票或印刷标记
senses.example: The envelope had no postage on it.
senses.exampleCN: 信封上没有贴邮票。
senses.why: Because the charge is called postage, the small piece of paper proving it was paid borrows the very same name.
senses.whyCN: 既然这笔费用叫 postage，用来证明已付款的那小张纸也就借用了同一个名称。

senses.title: The rates charged for mail by weight and distance
senses.definition: the set of rates a postal service charges according to weight, size and destination
senses.definitionCN: 邮政部门按重量、尺寸与目的地收取的一整套费用标准
senses.example: Rates of postage differ for letters and small parcels.
senses.exampleCN: 信件与小包裹的邮资标准不同。
senses.why: Once postage names a charge, it can also name the schedule of charges that a postal service applies.
senses.whyCN: postage 一旦能指一笔收费，也就能指邮政部门执行的一整套收费标准。

intro.en: Postage is post plus a suffix of charge, and the post inside it comes from posta, a station on a mail route.
intro.cn: postage 是 post 加表示费用的后缀构成，其中的 post 出自 posta，即邮路上的驿站。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or to place, and its participle positus, placed, lies behind the later word for a station.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置，其过去分词 positus（被放置的）是后来「驿站」一词的背后形式。

items.en: Posta named a road station where horses and messengers were changed, so mail could travel in stages.
items.cn: posta 指路上换马、换信使的站点，邮件因此可以分段传递。

items.en: French poste named both the station and the riders who carried letters, and English borrowed it in that double sense.
items.cn: 法语 poste 既指驿站，也指送信的骑手，英语把这两层意思一起借了进来。

items.en: Middle English post meant the mail and the service that moved it, the base on which the fee word was later built.
items.cn: 中古英语的 post 指邮件与运送邮件的机构，后来表示费用的词就建在这个基础上。

items.en: English added -age, a suffix of charge and belonging, to post and named the fee; the word is first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语给 post 加上表示「费用、归属」的后缀 -age 来指这笔钱；该词首次记录于十六世纪。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same post root; the second collects words for stamps, mail and fees, the field postage belongs to.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 post 词根上的词；近义组收邮票、邮件与费用这一词义场里的词。

entries.definition: The mail service or an upright pole, the root that postage is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 指邮政或柱子，是 postage 所由构成的基础词。

entries.definition: Relating to the mail service, built with the suffix -al.
entries.definitionCN: 加后缀 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」。

entries.definition: A card sent by mail without an envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 不装信封、直接邮寄的明信片。

entries.definition: A mark printed on mail to show when and where it was sent.
entries.definitionCN: 盖在邮件上、标明寄出时间与地点的邮戳。

entries.definition: A small piece of paper stuck on mail to pay the charge.
entries.definitionCN: 贴在邮件上用来付邮资的小纸片。

entries.definition: The act or cost of sending something by mail.
entries.definitionCN: 邮寄的行为或所需的花费。

entries.definition: A sum charged for a service.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项服务收取的费用。

entries.definition: Money charged for bringing goods to a buyer.
entries.definitionCN: 把货物送到买家手中所收的费用。

normalIntro.en: The word is a root meaning mail plus a suffix that regularly names a charge, which is why one noun covers a fee, a stamp and a rate table.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「邮政」词根加一个常用来表示费用的后缀，所以同一个名词能同时指费用、邮票与资费表。

normal.en: Postage is post plus -age; -age often names a fee, as it does in mileage or brokerage.
normal.cn: postage 是 post 加 -age；-age 常用来表示费用，mileage 与 brokerage 也是这样。

normal.en: The post inside comes from posta, a relay station where letters changed horses.
normal.cn: 里面的 post 出自 posta，即换马转递信件的驿站。

normal.en: Postage stamp keeps both halves: the fee and the small paper that proves it was paid.
normal.cn: postage stamp 两半都保留：费用，以及证明付过费的那小张纸。

normal.en: Postal and postage share a root but not a suffix: -al makes an adjective, -age makes a noun of charge.
normal.cn: postal 与 postage 同根而不同缀：-al 造形容词，-age 造表示费用的名词。

normal.en: Postage paid on an envelope means the sender has already covered the charge.
normal.cn: 信封上写着邮资已付，意思是寄件人已经把费用付清。

abstract.en: Postage is the price of distance, paid before the journey begins.
abstract.cn: 邮费是距离的价钱，在旅程开始之前就要付清。

abstract.en: A stamp is a receipt small enough to travel with the letter.
abstract.cn: 邮票是一张小到可以随信同行的收据。

abstract.en: One word covers a fee, a stamp and a rate table because a postal system needs all three to work.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指费用、邮票和资费表，因为邮政系统三者缺一不可。

examples.en: How much is the postage for this parcel?
examples.cn: 这个包裹的邮费是多少？

examples.en: The price includes postage and packing.
examples.cn: 这个价格包含邮费与包装费。

examples.en: She stuck a postage stamp on the corner of the envelope.
examples.cn: 她在信封角上贴了一张邮票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖尸贴纸」——把邮包剖开、贴上邮票，只为付那笔邮费；记住 postage 是邮费。

root: post（邮政，出自中世纪拉丁语 posta「驿站」）加表示费用与归属的后缀 -age 构成，字面即「邮政所收的钱」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the fee itself; from the fee the word extends to the stamps that pay it and to the whole table of rates.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义就是那笔费用；由费用再扩展到用来付款的邮票，以及整套收费标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter on a counter scale, a stamp in its corner and a postmark across it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封信放在柜台秤上，角上贴着邮票，上面盖着邮戳。

branches.en: coins counted out at a post office counter
branches.cn: 邮局柜台上一枚枚数出的硬币

branches.en: a stamp pressed into the corner of an envelope
branches.cn: 按在信封角上的邮票

branches.en: a chart listing prices by weight
branches.cn: 一张按重量列价的表

branches.en: a parcel marked with a paid stamp
branches.cn: 盖了邮资已付印记的包裹

branches.en: a sender comparing rates before choosing a box
branches.cn: 寄件人先比价再选箱子

intro.en: The word is a root meaning mail plus a suffix of charge; both parts come through French from Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是「邮政」词根加表示费用的后缀，两部分都经法语来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin posta, the station behind post, and the suffix -aticum behind French -age, together explain the shape of postage.
latinIntro.cn: post 背后的拉丁语 posta（驿站），以及法语 -age 背后的后缀 -aticum，共同解释了 postage 的形态。

definition_zh: 普遍的；广泛的；分布广的；广为流传的
definition_en: found or happening in many places or among many people over a large area
core_image: 一张大地图上，同一种颜色的斑点从一角蔓到另一角
scene: 地图上同一颜色的斑点从海边一路爬到山那边，几乎没有空白的地方。 There is widespread support for the new library among local families.
sceneCN: 这里 widespread 是「普遍的」（第 1 个义项：在许多地方或许多人中都能见到）；句意为当地家庭普遍支持新建图书馆。地图上从一角蔓到另一角的同色斑点，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 普遍的；分布广的；广为流传的

derivatives.zh: 宽的
广泛地
铺开；传播
不断扩大的

senses.title: Found in many places
senses.definition: existing in many places over an area, as a plant, a habit or a problem
senses.definitionCN: 在一片区域内许多地方都存在，如植物、习惯或问题
senses.example: There is widespread support for the new library among local families.
senses.exampleCN: 当地家庭普遍支持新建图书馆。
senses.why: The compound is literally spread wide, so the picture is a thing lying across a whole region.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词字面就是「铺得很宽」，画面是一件横卧在整个区域上的东西。

senses.title: Happening to many people
senses.definition: used of events, damage or illness that affect a large share of people
senses.definitionCN: 形容事件、破坏或疾病影响很大一部分人
senses.example: The storm caused widespread damage along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴给沿海带来大面积破坏。
senses.why: A storm does not choose one house, and the adjective marks damage that reaches everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 风暴不会只挑一栋房子，这个形容词标记的正是什么都波及到的损坏。

senses.title: Believed by many people
senses.definition: used of ideas, beliefs or reports that are held by a great many people
senses.definitionCN: 形容被众多人持有的观念、看法或报道
senses.example: It is a widespread belief that owls can see in total darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍认为猫头鹰能在全黑的夜里看见东西。
senses.why: An idea spreads like a seed across a field, so the same compound covers opinion.
senses.whyCN: 想法像种子一样撒满田野，于是同一个复合词也覆盖了意见。

senses.title: In general commercial use
senses.definition: used of a product, tool or method that has reached a large share of the market
senses.definitionCN: 形容产品或方法已进入大部分市场
senses.example: The technology became widespread only after the price fell.
senses.exampleCN: 这项技术直到价格下降后才被广泛使用。
senses.why: The word measures reach rather than depth, so it suits goods that are everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量的是覆盖而不深度，因此适用于到处都是的东西。

intro.en: Widespread is a clear modern compound of wide and the past participle spread, literally spread over a wide area.
intro.cn: widespread 是 wide 与过去分词 spread 的现代复合词，字面就是「铺得很宽」。

items.en: Wid meant broad, and spraedan meant to stretch out or scatter.
items.cn: wid 表示宽阔，spraedan 表示铺开、撒开。

items.en: The participle spred described a cloth or a rumour laid out over a surface.
items.cn: 分词 spred 描述铺在表面上的布或传开的谣言。

items.en: The two parts joined in the eighteenth century to describe things reaching across a region.
items.cn: 两部分在十八世纪合起来，用来描述横跨一片区域的事物。

items.en: Reporting of disease and weather made it a favourite word for damage and infection.
items.cn: 对疾病与天气的报道使它成为形容破坏与感染的爱用词。

items.en: It now also covers beliefs and technology, anything whose reach is the point.
items.cn: 如今它也覆盖信念与技术，凡是以「覆盖广度」为要点的事物都可使用。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds built on spread or wide, the second the words for general extent.
note.cn: 第一组收以 spread 或 wide 构成的复合词，第二组收表示普遍程度的词。

entries.definition: To stretch out or scatter over an area.
Having effects over a wide area, a close cousin.
The measuring element inside the compound.
Having read a lot, another hyphen-free compound.
Found often, in many places.
Affecting nearly all, not special.
True of everyone everywhere.

normalIntro.en: Widespread is easy to spell and easy to picture: take spread and put wide in front of it.
normalIntro.cn: widespread 既好拼又好想：把 spread 铺开，前面加个 wide。

normal.en: Spread is already flat, and wide makes it reach the edges.
normal.cn: spread 已经是平的，wide 让它一直铺到边上。

normal.en: The compound never changes form, so no comparison is needed.
normal.cn: 这个复合词形式不变，所以也不需要比较级。

normal.en: Damage, support and belief all lie across the same wide map.
normal.cn: 破坏、支持与信念都躺在同一张宽地图上。

normal.en: A rumour becomes widespread faster than a fact.
normal.cn: 谣言比事实更容易变得人人皆知。

normal.en: Widespread use means the tool is in every kitchen.
normal.cn: widespread use 说明这工具家家都有。

abstract.en: See one colour creep across a whole map.
abstract.cn: 看见一种颜色在大地图上慢慢爬开。

abstract.en: Feel a belief repeated in every shop you pass.
abstract.cn: 感觉每经过一家店都听见同一个看法。

abstract.en: Hear a whisper grow into a general roar.
abstract.cn: 听一句耳语长成一片轰鸣。

examples.en: There was widespread criticism of the decision.
examples.cn: 这个决定受到了广泛批评。

examples.en: Flooding caused widespread damage to the rice fields.
examples.cn: 洪水给稻田造成大面积破坏。

examples.en: Mobile payment is now widespread even in small towns.
examples.cn: 如今连小城镇也普遍使用移动支付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外的斯普瑞德」——外边到处都铺开了，所以很普遍。

root: wide（宽阔）+ spread（铺开）→ 十八世纪复合为 widespread；同族有 wide、widely、spread。

sensesIntro.en: The compound describes support that reaches many families, damage that covers a coast, a belief held by many, and a tool that is everywhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个复合词描述遍及许多家庭的支持、覆盖整条海岸的破坏、众人持有的看法，以及到处都在用的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one colour of dots creeping from one corner of a map to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一种颜色的斑点从地图一角爬到另一角。

branches.en: The support branch: families behind the new library.
branches.cn: 支持分支：支持新图书馆的众多家庭。

branches.en: The storm branch: damage along the whole coast.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：整条海岸的破坏。

branches.en: The belief branch: owls and the darkest night.
branches.cn: 看法分支：猫头鹰与最黑的夜。

branches.en: The market branch: a technology after the price fell.
branches.cn: 市场分支：降价后的技术。

branches.en: The reach branch: measuring breadth, not depth.
branches.cn: 覆盖分支：量的是广度，不是深度。

intro.en: Widespread is a transparent compound of two free words, and the first element wide does the whole job of measuring breadth.
intro.cn: widespread 是两个自由词构成的透明复合词，第一个成分 wide 承担了全部度量广度的任务。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed equivalents.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出借入的对应词。

items.exampleCN: 副词工作由 widely 承担。

latinEntries.example: It gives English vulgar in its old sense.

definition_zh: 享受；乐趣；享有
definition_en: the pleasure you get from something, or the legal use of a right or benefit
core_image: 老人闭着眼听唱片，手指跟着节拍轻敲扶手，脸上慢慢浮出笑
scene: 老人每天清晨在公园里拉琴，不为演出，只为拉琴本身的快乐。 Her enjoyment of music never depended on an audience.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoyment 是「享受；乐趣」（第 1 个义项：从某事物中获得的快乐）；句意：她对音乐的享受从来不依赖听众。

derivatives.zh: 享受；喜爱
令人愉快的
愉快地

senses.title: Pleasure from something
senses.definition: the feeling of pleasure that something gives you
senses.definitionCN: 某事物带给你的快乐感受
senses.example: He plays the piano purely for enjoyment.
senses.exampleCN: 他弹钢琴纯粹是为了乐趣。
senses.why: The -ment ending turns enjoy into the name of the pleasure itself.
senses.whyCN: -ment 词尾把 enjoy 变成「快乐本身」的名称。

senses.title: The use of a right or benefit
senses.definition: the legal or formal use of something you have a right to
senses.definitionCN: 对你有权拥有之物进行合法或正式的使用
senses.example: The tenants have quiet enjoyment of the property.
senses.exampleCN: 租户们可以安静地享有该房产。
senses.why: Enjoy also means to have the benefit of something, so enjoyment can name that possession and use.
senses.whyCN: enjoy 也有「享有」之意，所以 enjoyment 可以指这种拥有与使用。

senses.title: A source of pleasure
senses.definition: an activity or thing that gives you pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 带给你快乐的活动或事物
senses.example: Gardening is her chief enjoyment.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是她最大的乐事。
senses.why: The feeling and the thing that causes it are close enough for the same noun to cover both.
senses.whyCN: 感受与引起感受的事物足够接近，同一个名词可以兼指两者。

intro.en: Enjoyment is enjoy plus the noun ending -ment, naming the pleasure or the benefit enjoyed.
intro.cn: enjoyment 是 enjoy 加名词词尾 -ment，指所享受的快乐或享有的权益。

items.en: Gaudere means to rejoice, the distant source of joy.
items.cn: gaudere 意为欢欣，是 joy 的远源。

items.en: Enjoir means to take pleasure in or to have the use of something.
items.cn: enjoir 意为从某物获得快乐，或享有某物。

items.en: Middle English enjoy carries both the pleasure and the legal use senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 enjoy 兼有「快乐」与「合法使用」两种含义。

items.en: Enjoyment appears as the state or act named by the verb.
items.cn: enjoyment 出现，表示动词所指的状态或行为。

items.en: Legal writing uses quiet enjoyment for undisturbed possession.
items.cn: 法律写作使用 quiet enjoyment 表示不受干扰地占有。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday pleasure sense as the main one.
items.cn: 现代英语以日常的「乐趣」义为主要义项。

note.en: Enjoyment is the noun of enjoy, and it sits near words for pleasure, delight, and satisfaction.
note.cn: enjoyment 是 enjoy 的名词，与 pleasure、delight、satisfaction 等词相邻。

entries.definition: to take pleasure in something
giving pleasure
a feeling of great happiness
a feeling of happiness or satisfaction
great pleasure
the feeling of being pleased with a result
the pleasure of having a desire met

normalIntro.en: Enjoyment is enjoy plus -ment, so the noun names the pleasure that the verb produces.
normalIntro.cn: enjoyment 是 enjoy 加 -ment，名词指动词所产生的快乐。

normal.en: Enjoy plus -ment: the state of enjoying something.
normal.cn: enjoy 加 -ment：享受某物的状态。

normal.en: For enjoyment is the phrase that marks an activity done for fun.
normal.cn: for enjoyment 标出「为乐趣而做」的活动。

normal.en: Derive enjoyment from is the formal way to say get pleasure from.
normal.cn: derive enjoyment from 是 get pleasure from 的正式说法。

normal.en: Quiet enjoyment is a legal phrase for undisturbed use of property.
normal.cn: quiet enjoyment 是表示不受干扰使用房产的法律短语。

normal.en: Compare enjoyable: enjoyment is the feeling, enjoyable is the cause.
normal.cn: 对比 enjoyable：enjoyment 是感受，enjoyable 是原因。

abstract.en: Picture someone listening to a record with eyes closed and fingers tapping.
abstract.cn: 想象有人闭眼听唱片，手指轻敲节拍。

abstract.en: Imagine a gardener who forgets the time among the plants.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁在花草间忘了时间。

abstract.en: Think of a meal eaten slowly because every bite is worth it.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿慢慢吃的饭，因为每一口都值得。

examples.en: She reads poetry for enjoyment, not for exams.
examples.cn: 她读诗是为了乐趣，不是为了考试。

examples.en: The children shouted with enjoyment at the puppet show.
examples.cn: 孩子们看木偶戏时高兴地叫喊。

examples.en: The agreement guarantees quiet enjoyment of the flat.
examples.cn: 协议保障对这套公寓的安静享有权。

dict_mnemonic.text: enjoy（享受）+ -ment（名词词尾）＝享受、乐趣；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: enjoy（享受、享有，源自拉丁语 gaudere「欢欣」）+ 名词词尾 -ment，指享受带来的快乐，或对权益的合法享有。

sensesIntro.en: The pleasure comes first, then the legal use of a benefit, then the activity that produces the pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是快乐，再是对权益的合法使用，最后是产生快乐的活动本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pleasure held and used, like a right one is free to exercise.
core.cn: 核心意象：把快乐握在手中使用，就像行使一项自由拥有的权利。

branches.en: The feeling of pleasure is the main everyday sense.
branches.cn: 快乐感受，是主要的日常义项。

branches.en: Legal use of a right is the formal possessive sense.
branches.cn: 对权益的合法使用，是正式的「享有」义项。

branches.en: The activity that gives pleasure becomes a source of enjoyment.
branches.cn: 带来快乐的活动，成为「乐事」。

branches.en: Pleasure and its source are named by the same noun.
branches.cn: 快乐与其来源由同一个名词命名。

branches.en: Feeling pleasure and using a benefit both describe a good held by someone.
branches.cn: 感受快乐与使用权益都描述某人所拥有的好处。

intro.en: Enjoyment is a transparent English noun built from enjoy plus -ment.
intro.cn: enjoyment 是 enjoy 加 -ment 构成的、构词透明的英语名词。

latinIntro.en: The base enjoy comes from Latin gaudere, to rejoice, through Old French enjoir.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 enjoy 经古法语 enjoir 来自拉丁语 gaudere（欢欣）。

items.example: Enjoy is the base of enjoyment.
items.exampleCN: enjoy 是 enjoyment 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.exampleCN: enjoyment 由 enjoy 与 -ment 合成。
enjoyable 共享 enjoy 词干。

items.example: Joy shares the Latin root of enjoy.
items.exampleCN: joy 与 enjoy 共享拉丁词根。

items.example: Gaudere is the deepest root of enjoyment.
items.exampleCN: gaudere 是 enjoyment 最深的词根。

items.example: En- opens the base verb enjoy.
items.exampleCN: en- 出现在基础动词 enjoy 开头。

definition_zh: 彻底地；完全地；认真地；极其
definition_en: in a complete and careful way, with every part attended to, or to a very great degree
core_image: 把柜子从顶板擦到底板，每一格都擦过一遍
scene: 搬家前打扫空房，主人连门框顶端和窗轨凹槽都不放过。 She went through the flat thoroughly before the new tenants arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 thoroughly 是「彻底地、无一遗漏地」（第 1 个义项：每个角落都处理到）；句意为新房客到来前她把公寓彻底收拾了一遍。

pos.zh: 彻底地；全面地；认真仔细地

forms.label: 原级（形容词 thoroughly 的形容词形式）

derivatives.zh: 由副词去掉后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「彻底的；全面的」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「彻底；周密」
thorough 与 fare 的古老复合词，义为「大道；通路」

senses.title: In a complete and careful way
senses.definition: in a way that covers every part or detail, so that nothing is left out
senses.definitionCN: 以涵盖每个部分或细节、无所遗漏的方式
senses.example: The mechanic thoroughly checked the brakes before the car left the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工在车出厂前把刹车彻底检查了一遍。
senses.why: The word is the adverb of thorough, the old twin of through: something done thoroughly has been carried all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 thorough 的副词，而 thorough 是 through 的古老孪生词：彻底做完的事，就是被一路走穿到底的事。

senses.title: With great care and attention
senses.titleCN: 认真仔细地；一丝不苟地
senses.definition: with careful attention to correctness and detail, of a way of working or thinking
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或思考方式认真细致、注重正确与细节
senses.example: You should read the contract thoroughly before signing it.
senses.exampleCN: 签字前你应该认真通读合同。
senses.why: Care walks the whole road: the adverb marks the walker who leaves no step untaken.
senses.whyCN: 用心要走过整条路：这个副词标记的是不肯省下任何一步的走法。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to a very great degree, especially with verbs of feeling and opinion
senses.definitionCN: 程度很高，尤与表示感受和看法的动词连用
senses.example: I thoroughly enjoyed the concert last night.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚的音乐会我听得十分过瘾。
senses.why: Completeness slides from the task to the feeling: a pleasure that is complete is one felt thoroughly.
senses.whyCN: 「彻底」从任务滑到感受上：完整的快乐就是被彻底感受到的快乐。

senses.title: Utterly, in a bad sense
senses.titleCN: 完全地；十足地（多含贬义）
senses.definition: completely and absolutely, often before a negative judgement
senses.definitionCN: 完全地、绝对地，常用于否定评价之前
senses.example: The plan was thoroughly misguided from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划从一开始就完全走错了方向。
senses.why: The same completeness can measure failure or folly: the depth of the error is what the adverb reports.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「彻底」也能衡量失败与愚蠢：这个副词报告的是错误的深度。

intro.en: Thoroughly is the adverb built on thorough, the adjective twin of through; the whole family goes back to one Germanic root for passing from one side to the other.
intro.cn: thoroughly 是建立在 thorough 之上的副词，而 thorough 是 through 的形容词孪生词；整个词族都源自同一个表示「从一侧到另一侧」的日耳曼词根。

items.en: The old root behind through meant from one side to the other, with an image of a door or passage being crossed.
items.cn: through 背后的古老词根意为「从一侧到另一侧」，带着「穿过门或通道」的意象。

items.en: Old English had the preposition and adverb for passing through, and a compound meaning going right through, hence complete.
items.cn: 古英语已有表示「穿过」的介词与副词，并有「直贯而过」的复合词，引申为完全。

items.en: Middle English split the spellings: through kept the motion job, thorough took the completeness job, and -ly made the adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写分化：through 保留运动义，thorough 接管「彻底」义，加 -ly 构成副词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century onward, thoroughly settled as the standard adverb for complete and careful action.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，thoroughly 固定为表示「彻底、细致」动作的标准副词。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to degree, as in thoroughly enjoy, where the sense is intensity rather than coverage.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到程度，如 thoroughly enjoy，此时表示强度而非覆盖范围。

note.en: The first group lines up the spelling family around thorough; the second compares adverbs and adjectives of completeness and care.
note.cn: 第一组排开 thorough 周边的拼写家族；第二组比较表示彻底与用心的副词和形容词。

entries.definition: Complete and careful, with nothing left out; the adjective this adverb is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的；全面的（thoroughly 所依附的形容词）

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the motion twin that shares the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；通过（与 thorough 同根的运动义孪生词）

entries.definition: In every part of a place or period; through plus out.
entries.definitionCN: 遍及；自始至终（through 与 out 复合）

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being complete and careful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「彻底、周密」，由 thorough 加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: In every part; the most general adverb of wholeness, with no image of care.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地（最一般的「完整」副词，不带用心的意象）

entries.definition: Wholly, with nothing excluded; often used with negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；全部地（常与否定词连用）

entries.definition: With attention to avoiding mistakes; it stresses caution rather than coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细地；小心地（强调谨慎而非覆盖面）

entries.definition: Completely, almost always before a negative quality.
entries.definitionCN: 十足地；完全地（多修饰负面品质）

normalIntro.en: Real hooks from the word family: thorough, through, -ly, and the degree sense.
normalIntro.cn: 来自词族的真实钩子：thorough、through、后缀 -ly，以及程度用法。

normal.en: Thoroughly is thorough plus -ly, the ordinary way English turns an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: thoroughly 就是 thorough 加 -ly，英语把形容词变副词最常见的方式。

normal.en: A thorough search goes through everything, and thoroughly means doing it that way.
normal.cn: 彻底的搜查会把每样东西都翻 through，thoroughly 就是「以那种方式」。

normal.en: Thoroughly checked means no part was skipped.
normal.cn: 彻底检查过的意思是没有哪一部分被跳过。

normal.en: With feelings the word marks depth: thoroughly enjoy, thoroughly agree.
normal.cn: 与感受连用时它标记深度：十分享受、完全同意。

normal.en: With negative words it marks total failure: thoroughly wrong, thoroughly misguided.
normal.cn: 与负面词连用时它标记全盘失败：完全错误、彻底走偏。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp carried into every corner of a dark room until no shadow is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被提进暗房的每个角落，直到不留一丝阴影。

abstract.en: Thoroughly is the sound of a job finished on the last step, not the middle one.
abstract.cn: thoroughly 是一件事在最后一步而非中途完成的声响。

abstract.en: Complete attention, complete feeling and complete failure all wear the same adverb.
abstract.cn: 完整的注意力、完整的感受、彻底的失败，戴的是同一个副词。

examples.en: She thoroughly enjoyed her first week at the new job.
examples.cn: 她在新工作的第一周过得十分愉快。

examples.en: The room was thoroughly cleaned before the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到来前房间被彻底打扫过。

examples.en: I thoroughly disagree with that conclusion.
examples.cn: 我完全不同意那个结论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟若利」——瑟缩着把每寸地板都擦利落 → 彻底地

root: thoroughly = thorough（与 through 同源的日耳曼词根，意为「贯穿」，引申为「彻底」）+ 副词后缀 -ly；古英语同根词表示「直贯而过」，中古英语拼写分化后 thorough 专表「完全」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of thoroughly all measure completeness, applied to a task, a way of working, a feeling, or a bad judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: thoroughly 的四个义项都在衡量「完整」，分别用在任务、工作方式、感受与糟糕的判断上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp carried into every corner of a room until no shadow remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被提进房间的每个角落，直到不留阴影。

branches.en: The task: every part covered, nothing skipped.
branches.cn: 任务线：每部分都覆盖，无一跳过。

branches.en: The worker: care that walks every step of the reading or check.
branches.cn: 做事者线：用心走完阅读或检查的每一步。

branches.en: The feeling: pleasure or agreement felt to the full.
branches.cn: 感受线：快乐或赞同被完整地感受到。

branches.en: The error: completeness measuring how deep the mistake goes.
branches.cn: 错误线：彻底衡量错误有多深。

branches.en: Coverage and care both come from the road image inside thorough.
branches.cn: 覆盖面与用心都来自 thorough 内部的道路意象。

intro.en: Thoroughly carries only native English endings: the adjective -ly pivot and the noun -ness.
intro.cn: thoroughly 只带英语本土词缀：构成副词的 -ly，以及构成名词的 -ness。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 它把 thorough 变成 thoroughly。

items.meaning: a public road through a place
items.example: The avenue is a busy thoroughfare.

items.meaning: from one side to the other
items.example: The train went through the tunnel.

items.exampleCN: 他们要求一场彻底的改革。

definition_zh: 有毒的；含毒的；有毒腺的；吃了会中毒的；恶毒的
definition_en: containing or producing a poison that can harm or kill, and figuratively full of bitterness and ill will
core_image: 贴着骷髅标签的棕色瓶子，盖子一开就冒出白气
scene: 实验室的通风柜前，助手把护目镜又压紧了一点，才去拧那只棕色瓶子的盖子。 The label warns that the fumes are poisonous if the bottle is left open.
sceneCN: 这里是「含有毒物的、有毒的」（第 1 个义项：物质本身含毒）；句意为标签警告说，瓶子敞着放，里面冒出的气体就是有毒的。画面里有通风柜、护目镜和一只棕色试剂瓶。

pos.zh: 有毒的；含毒的；有毒腺的；恶毒的

derivatives.zh: 由 poisonous 去掉形容词后缀 -ous 得到的名词，义为「毒药；毒物」
与名词同形的动词，义为「下毒；毒害」
由 poison 加 -ing 构成，义为「下毒；中毒」
由 poisonous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有毒地；恶毒地」

senses.title: Containing a substance that harms or kills
senses.definition: containing or giving off a poison that can damage the body or cause death
senses.definitionCN: 含有或散发出能损害身体、甚至致死的毒物
senses.example: The tank was sealed because the gas inside was poisonous.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子被密封起来，因为里面的气体有毒。
senses.why: The suffix -ous says that something is full of what the noun names, so the adjective first describes what the material contains rather than whom it hurts.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 表示「充满名词所指之物」，所以这个形容词先说的是材料里含有什么，而不是它伤了谁。

senses.title: Producing venom and able to inject it
senses.titleCN: 有毒腺的；会咬人放毒的
senses.definition: used of an animal that makes venom in its body and can pass it on by biting or stinging
senses.definitionCN: 用于体内制造毒液、并能通过咬或蜇把毒液注入对方身体的动物
senses.example: Only a few of the snakes in this region are poisonous.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带只有少数几种蛇是有毒的。
senses.why: English uses one adjective for a swallowed poison and for injected venom, because in both cases a living body is carrying a dose of harm inside it.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个形容词覆盖吞下去的毒和被注入的毒液，因为两种情形都是一个活体身上带着一份会伤人的剂量。

senses.title: Unsafe to eat
senses.definition: used of food, berries or mushrooms that make a person ill or kill them once swallowed
senses.definitionCN: 用于一旦吃下就会让人生病或致命的食物、浆果与蘑菇
senses.example: She threw the berries away because some of them were poisonous.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那些浆果扔了，因为其中有些是有毒的。
senses.why: Once the adjective describes what a thing contains rather than how it attacks, it settles easily on food, where the danger appears only after swallowing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个形容词说的是「东西里含有什么」而不是「它怎么攻击」，它就很容易落到食物上，因为那里的危险要等吞下去之后才出现。

senses.title: Full of bitterness and ill will
senses.definition: full of hatred or malice, said of remarks, feelings or the mood of a place
senses.definitionCN: 充满憎恨或恶意，用于言语、情绪或一个地方的氛围
senses.example: The meeting turned poisonous once the two managers began to trade blame.
senses.exampleCN: 两位经理一开始互相推卸责任，会议的气氛就变得充满敌意。
senses.why: Poison works unseen and spreads through whatever carries it, so the same word describes words or moods that infect everyone who breathes them in.
senses.whyCN: 毒物看不见，却会顺着载着它的东西扩散，于是同一个词也形容话语或情绪，谁吸进去谁就被感染。

intro.en: Poisonous is the noun poison with the adjective suffix -ous, and poison itself goes back to a Latin word for a drink that could heal or kill.
intro.cn: poisonous 是名词 poison 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成的，而 poison 本身源自一个既可治病也可致命的拉丁语「饮剂」词。

items.en: Potio meant a drink, especially a measured draught, and the same word could name a healing cup or a harmful one.
items.cn: potio 意为「饮料」，尤指按量配好的一剂，同一个词既能指治病的药饮，也能指害人的毒饮。

items.en: The verb potare meant to drink, and it stands behind the drink words of this family, including English potable.
items.cn: 动词 potare 意为「喝」，这一族与饮用有关的词都由它而来，英语的 potable 也在其中。

items.en: Old French poison still meant a drink or potion, but in medieval use it was most often a harmful draught handed to a victim.
items.cn: 古法语 poison 仍指饮料或药剂，但在中世纪的用法里，它多半指递给受害者的一杯毒饮。

items.en: Middle English borrowed poison as a noun for a deadly substance, and English then added -ous to name the quality of containing it.
items.cn: 中古英语把 poison 借作名词，指致命的物质；英语随后加 -ous，用来指「含有这种物质」的性质。

items.en: Modern English keeps both noun and adjective and widens the adjective to venomous animals, spoiled food and bitter speech.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留名词与形容词，并把形容词扩展到有毒的动物、变质的食物和刻薄的言辞。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the drink words of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things that harm the body.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族里与「饮剂」有关的词；近义组收表示「伤害身体」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun the adjective is built on: a substance that harms or kills.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词所由来的名词：能伤害或杀死人的物质。

entries.definition: A drink with supposed magical or medicinal power, from the Latin word for a draught.
entries.definitionCN: 据称有魔力或药效的饮剂，源自拉丁语中表示「一饮」的词。

entries.definition: Safe or fit to drink, built on the Latin verb meaning to drink.
entries.definitionCN: 可以安全饮用的，建立在拉丁语「喝」这一动词上。

entries.definition: The act of giving poison, or the illness that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 下毒的行为，或随之而来的中毒。

entries.definition: Poisonous in a scientific or medical register, often of chemicals.
entries.definitionCN: 科学或医学语境里的「有毒」，多指化学品。

entries.definition: Producing venom and injecting it by bite or sting.
entries.definitionCN: 产生毒液并通过咬或蜇注入的。

entries.definition: Harmful to health, especially of fumes or smells.
entries.definitionCN: 有害健康的，多指气体或气味。

entries.definition: Able to cause damage of any kind, weaker than poisonous.
entries.definitionCN: 能造成任何伤害的，语气比 poisonous 轻。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is a Latin word for a draught wearing the suffix of fullness, and both halves still show in how it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁语「一饮」披上表示「充满」的后缀，两半至今都能从用法里看出来。

normal.en: -ous means full of, so poisonous is literally full of poison and describes what a thing carries.
normal.cn: -ous 表示「充满」，所以 poisonous 字面就是「充满毒」，说的是东西里装着什么。

normal.en: Poison and potion share the Latin word for a drink, which is why the old image of poison is a cup, not a wound.
normal.cn: poison 与 potion 共用拉丁语中「饮料」这个词，所以毒最古老的画面是一只杯子，而不是一道伤口。

normal.en: A poisonous snake carries venom in its body, while poisonous gas fills a room; English lets one adjective cover both.
normal.cn: poisonous snake 把毒液带在身上，poisonous gas 把毒气充满房间，英语让一个形容词同时管这两种情形。

normal.en: Poisoning is the noun for the event, and poisonously is the adverb for the manner, so the family covers thing, act and style.
normal.cn: poisoning 是表示事件的名词，poisonously 是表示方式副词，这一族词因此覆盖了物、事与姿态。

normal.en: Potable comes from the same verb for drinking but means safe to drink, showing that relatives can take opposite sides.
normal.cn: potable 出自同一个「喝」的动词，意思却是「能安全饮用」，可见同族词可以站到相反的一边。

abstract.en: A word that starts as a drink reminds us that harm often arrives in something we are glad to receive.
abstract.cn: 一个从「饮料」起步的词提醒人：伤害常常藏在一样我们乐于接受的东西里。

abstract.en: Because poison spreads through a carrier, the same adjective can describe air, a snake and a sentence.
abstract.cn: 因为毒要靠载体扩散，同一个形容词才能既形容空气，又形容蛇，还形容一句话。

abstract.en: The step from substance to mood is short: what cannot be seen is what most easily fills a room.
abstract.cn: 从物质到情绪的跨度很短：看不见的东西，最容易充满一个房间。

examples.en: The tank was sealed because the gas inside was poisonous.
examples.cn: 罐子被密封起来，因为里面的气体有毒。

examples.en: She threw the berries away because some of them were poisonous.
examples.cn: 她把那些浆果扔了，因为其中有些是有毒的。

examples.en: A poisonous silence filled the room after his remark.
examples.cn: 他那一句话之后，房间里弥漫着敌意的沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼伊怎死」——毒液泼到人身上，沾上就难逃一死，这就是 poisonous 的有毒。

root: 拉丁语 potio（饮剂）与 potare（喝）经古法语 poison 进入英语，先指饮下的一剂，后专指毒物；再加 -ous 构成 poisonous。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a thing that carries harm inside it; from that come the venomous animal, the dangerous food, and finally the bitter mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「里面带着伤害的东西」；由此分出带毒液的动物、危险的食物，最后是刻薄的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown bottle with a skull label, white vapour rising as the cap comes off.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着骷髅标签的棕色瓶子，盖子一开就冒出白气。

branches.en: a sealed jar marked with a skull
branches.cn: 贴着骷髅标记的密封罐

branches.en: a snake coiled with its head raised
branches.cn: 盘起身子昂起头的蛇

branches.en: a child pulled back from wild berries
branches.cn: 孩子被拉回来，没去摘野果

branches.en: a room going quiet after a cruel remark
branches.cn: 一句刻薄话之后安静下来的房间

branches.en: a warning sign nailed beside a well
branches.cn: 钉在水井旁的警示牌

intro.en: A Latin word for a drink, its verb, and one English suffix of fullness hold this word together, and the family splits into the substance, the act and the manner.
intro.cn: 一个表示「饮剂」的拉丁名词、它的动词，加上一个表示「充满」的英语后缀，撑起这个词；这一族再分出物质、行为与方式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 现象；迹象；非凡的人或事；奇才
definition_en: a fact or event that can be observed, especially one that is unusual or not yet explained; also an extraordinary person or thing
core_image: 黑暗中忽然亮起一点，被眼睛稳稳接住
scene: 球状闪电这种现象，科学家至今仍无法解释。 Scientists still cannot explain the phenomenon of ball lightning.
sceneCN: 这里 phenomenon 是「可观察但尚未解释的事实」（第 1 个义项：现象）；句意：科学家至今无法解释球状闪电这一现象。场景要点：异常、被观测到、原因未知；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 现象；迹象；非凡的人或事

forms.label: 复数（指非凡人物时偶用）

derivatives.zh: 现象的；非凡的；惊人的
非凡地；惊人地
现象学（哲学分支）
现象主义（认为人只能认识现象）

senses.title: An observable fact or event
senses.titleCN: 现象：能被观察到的某事
senses.definition: a fact or event that can be observed, especially one whose cause is not yet understood
senses.definitionCN: 可以被观察到的事实或事件，尤指原因尚未被理解的那种
senses.example: The northern lights are a phenomenon seen near the poles.
senses.exampleCN: 北极光是在极地附近能看到的一种现象。
senses.why: Greek phainomenon means that which appears. Anything that shows itself to the senses qualifies, whether or not we can explain it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phainomenon 意为“显现出来的东西”。凡向感官显现的都可算，无论我们能否解释它。

senses.title: Something unusual or unexplained
senses.titleCN: 异象：解释不了的那件事
senses.definition: an event that is strange, rare, or not yet explained by science
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪的、罕见的、或科学尚未解释的事件
senses.example: Reports of the phenomenon spread faster than any explanation could.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这一异象的报道传播得比任何解释都快。
senses.why: The word's everyday weight shifted toward the unusual: if it appears and we cannot account for it, we call it a phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的日常重心转向“不寻常”：如果它显现了而我们说不清，就称它为 phenomenon。

senses.title: An event of the natural world
senses.titleCN: 自然现象：大地自己演出的那一幕
senses.definition: a regularly occurring event of the physical world, such as weather, tides, or growth
senses.definitionCN: 物理世界中规律发生的事件，如天气、潮汐或生长
senses.example: Migration is a phenomenon driven by season and food supply.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙是由季节和食物供给驱动的自然现象。
senses.why: Nature is the first place where things show themselves without human arrangement, so natural events became the model case.
senses.whyCN: 自然界是最早出现“无需人为安排就自行显现”的地方，因此自然事件成了典范情形。

senses.title: Philosophy: an object of experience
senses.titleCN: 哲学：呈现给意识的对象
senses.definition: in philosophy, anything that appears to consciousness, as opposed to the thing as it is in itself
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上指呈现于意识中的一切，以区别于物自身
senses.example: Kant argued that we know phenomena, not things in themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 康德主张我们认识的是现象，而非物自体。
senses.why: Philosophy kept the literal Greek sense: the phenomenon is exactly what appears, and the question is what lies behind the appearance.
senses.whyCN: 哲学保留了希腊本义：现象正是显现出来的那个东西，问题在于显现背后还有什么。

senses.title: Medicine: a sign or symptom
senses.definition: a sign or symptom that can be observed in a patient and points to a condition
senses.definitionCN: 在病人身上可以观察到、并指向某种病情的体征或症状
senses.example: Raynaud's phenomenon makes the fingers turn white in the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 雷诺现象使手指在寒冷中变白。
senses.why: A symptom is something that shows itself on the body. Medicine names the visible sign rather than the hidden cause.
senses.whyCN: 症状就是显现在身体上的东西。医学命名的是可见的征象，而不是隐藏的病因。

senses.title: An extraordinary person or thing
senses.titleCN: 奇人奇物：本身就是一件异象
senses.definition: a person or thing that is so remarkable that it seems to belong to a different order
senses.definitionCN: 非凡到仿佛属于另一类事物的人或物
senses.example: By fifteen she was a phenomenon in the chess world.
senses.exampleCN: 十五岁时她已是国际象棋界的奇才。
senses.why: If a person appears among ordinary people the way a marvel appears among ordinary events, the same word fits.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人出现在常人之中，就像奇观出现在寻常事件之中，同一个词就适用。

senses.title: A class of observable facts
senses.titleCN: 现象总称：成类的一批显现
senses.definition: the whole range of observable facts in a field, usually in the plural phenomena
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域内可观察事实的总和，通常用复数 phenomena
senses.example: The book surveys electrical phenomena in the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书综述了大气中的电现象。
senses.why: Greek plural phenomena was borrowed along with the singular. English uses the plural for a set of related appearances studied together.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语复数 phenomena 与单数一同被借入。英语用复数指一组放在一起研究的相关显现。

senses.title: A wonder to be witnessed
senses.titleCN: 奇观：值得亲眼一看的显现
senses.definition: something impressive that draws attention and seems worth seeing for itself
senses.definitionCN: 引人注目、本身值得一看的了不起之物
senses.example: The total eclipse was a phenomenon no one in the crowd would forget.
senses.exampleCN: 那次日全食是人群中无人会忘记的奇观。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply 'that which shows'. When what shows is overwhelming, the word slides toward spectacle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层只是“显现出来的东西”。当显现之物压倒地引人注目时，词义便滑向“奇观”。

intro.en: Phenomenon is a Greek philosophical term carried into English through Latin. Its base verb means to bring something into the light, and its spelling still carries the Greek plural.
intro.cn: phenomenon 是一个经拉丁语传入英语的希腊哲学术语。其底层动词意为“把某物带到光下”，其拼写至今保留希腊语复数。

items.en: Phainein meant 'to bring to light, show'. It descends from PIE *bha- 'to shine', the same source as English beacon and the root behind emphasis and fantasy.
items.cn: phainein 意为“带到光下、显现”。它源自原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”，与英语 beacon 以及 emphasis、fantasy 的词根同源。

items.en: The passive participle of phainesthai 'to appear' was phainomenon, literally 'that which appears'. Philosophers used it for whatever is given to the senses.
items.cn: phainesthai“显现”的被动分词是 phainomenon，字面即“显现出来的东西”。哲学家用它指一切呈现给感官之物。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek word as phaenomenon, keeping the philosophical sense. The ae spelling survives in the English plural phenomena.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊词借作 phaenomenon，保留哲学含义。其中的 ae 拼法在英语复数 phenomena 里仍有痕迹。

items.en: English records phenomenon in the 1570s as a learned term. The plural phenomena was borrowed with it, which is why it does not follow the regular English -s pattern.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 70 年代把 phenomenon 记录为学术用语，复数 phenomena 一并借入，所以它不按英语常规加 -s。

items.en: The sense 'extraordinary occurrence' is recorded in 1771, and the philosophical sense tied to Kant's usage spreads in the 1780s and after.
items.cn: “非凡事件”这一义项记录于 1771 年；与康德用法相关的哲学义在 18 世纪 80 年代及以后传播开来。

items.en: Modern English uses the singular for one event and phenomena for several. The informal plural phenomenons appears mainly for the 'remarkable person' sense and is often criticized.
items.cn: 现代英语用单数指一个事件，用 phenomena 指多个。非正式的 phenomenons 主要用于“非凡人物”义，且常受批评。

note.en: The first group shows the same Greek root in different dress. The second group collects words for things that happen or things that are seen.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个希腊词根的不同装束。第二组收表示“发生之事”或“被看见之物”的词。

entries.definition: the Greek plural of phenomenon. It is a plural noun, not a singular, so one should not say a phenomena.
entries.definitionCN: phenomenon 的希腊式复数。它是复数名词而非单数，因此不应说 a phenomena。

entries.definition: relating to phenomena, or extraordinary. The adjective adds -al to the stem phenomen-.
entries.definitionCN: 与现象有关的，或非凡的。形容词由词干 phenomen- 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: a ghost or an illusion. It comes from Greek phantasma, from phainein 'to show', the same root as phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 幽灵或幻象。它来自希腊语 phantasma，源于 phainein“显现”，与 phenomenon 同根。

entries.definition: an illusion or a product of imagination. It preserves more of the Greek phantasma than phantom does.
entries.definitionCN: 幻象或想象的产物。它比 phantom 保留了更多希腊语 phantasma 的原形。

entries.definition: something that happens. Event is neutral; phenomenon adds the idea of being observed and often of being puzzling.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的事情。event 中性；phenomenon 多出“被观察到”以及“常令人费解”的意思。

entries.definition: something that takes place. Occurrence simply records that it happened, without implying study or wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的事。occurrence 只记录它发生了，不含研究或惊奇的意味。

entries.definition: something that causes wonder. Marvel stresses the observer's amazement; phenomenon can be neutral and scientific.
entries.definitionCN: 引起惊奇的事物。marvel 强调观察者的惊叹；phenomenon 可以是中性的、科学的。

entries.definition: something that is seen, especially something unusual. Sight focuses on the visual impression, phenomenon on the fact observed.
entries.definitionCN: 所见之物，尤指不寻常的。sight 侧重视觉印象，phenomenon 侧重被观察的事实。

entries.definition: something known to be true. Fact is about truth claims; phenomenon is about appearance to an observer.
entries.definitionCN: 已知为真之事。fact 关乎真假判断；phenomenon 关乎对观察者的显现。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the light in the dark, the Greek plural, the Kantian split, the medical sign, and the child prodigy.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：黑暗中的光、希腊式复数、康德的分野、医学体征、少年奇才。

normal.en: Phenomenon = something that switches on in the dark and the eye catches it. Phan- in Greek means to show.
normal.cn: phenomenon＝在黑暗中亮起、被眼睛接住的东西。希腊语 phan- 就是“显现”。

normal.en: One phenomenon, two phenomena. Treat the -a as a Greek passport stamp, not as a mistake.
normal.cn: 一个 phenomenon，两个 phenomena。把词尾的 -a 看成希腊护照上的章，而不是拼写错误。

normal.en: Kant's slogan: we see phenomena, we never see the thing itself. The word is literally 'the appearing'.
normal.cn: 康德的口号：我们看见现象，看不见物自体。这个词字面就是“显现者”。

normal.en: A doctor reads phenomena on the body: white fingers in the cold are a phenomenon pointing to a hidden cause.
normal.cn: 医生读身体上的现象：寒冷中发白的手指就是一个指向隐藏病因的 phenomenon。

normal.en: Call a fifteen-year-old chess genius a phenomenon and you are saying she appears among us like a marvel among events.
normal.cn: 把十五岁的棋童称为 phenomenon，等于说她出现在我们中间，就像奇观出现在寻常事件中。

abstract.en: A phenomenon is the world's surface; the thing in itself is the world's depth. The word marks the limit of what can be shown.
abstract.cn: 现象是世界的表面，物自体是世界的深处。这个词标记的是“能被显现”的边界。

abstract.en: What counts as a phenomenon depends on who is looking and with what instrument; the observed is never wholly separate from the observer.
abstract.cn: 什么算作现象，取决于谁在看、用什么在看；被观察者从不与观察者完全分离。

abstract.en: Naming a phenomenon is the first act of science and already a theory: to pick it out is to decide what matters.
abstract.cn: 命名一个现象是科学的第一步，也已经是理论：挑出它，就是决定了什么才算重要。

examples.en: The migration of monarch butterflies is a phenomenon that still puzzles biologists.
examples.cn: 帝王蝶迁徙是至今仍让生物学家困惑的现象。

examples.en: In the 1960s the Beatles became a global phenomenon, not merely a band.
examples.cn: 20 世纪 60 年代，披头士成了全球性现象，而不仅仅是一支乐队。

examples.en: Phenomena observed at one temperature do not always hold at another.
examples.cn: 在某一温度下观察到的现象，未必在另一温度下成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费诺米农”——费诺在米农面前亮出一盏灯，众人看见一个现象（phenomenon）

root: 希腊语 phainein“显现、照亮”→ phainomenon“显现出来的东西”→ 晚期拉丁 phaenomenon → 英语 phenomenon；与 phase、emphasis、phantom、fantasy 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means what shows itself. From that base it spreads in two directions: toward the scientific fact to be explained, and toward the marvel that overwhelms the observer. The plural phenomena is Greek, not English.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“显现出来的东西”。由此向两个方向展开：一是待解释的科学事实，二是压倒地引人惊叹的奇观。复数 phenomena 是希腊式的，不是英语式的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a point of light in the dark, appearing to an eye that did not make it.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中的一点光，向一只并未制造它的眼睛显现。

branches.en: OBSERVATION: the neutral fact, natural or social, that anyone can notice.
branches.cn: 观察：中性的、任何人都能注意到的事实，自然的或社会的。

branches.en: PUZZLE: the same fact weighted with strangeness because no explanation is available.
branches.cn: 谜团：同一事实因缺乏解释而被加上了“怪异”的重量。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: appearance as such, set against the thing in itself.
branches.cn: 哲学：显现本身，与物自体相对而立。

branches.en: WITNESS: the sign read on a body and the spectacle watched by a crowd — appearance as evidence or as show.
branches.cn: 见证：身上读出的征候与众人围观的奇观——显现作为证据或作为演出。

branches.en: CLASS: a remarkable being, and the plural set of appearances studied together.
branches.cn: 类别：非凡的存在者，以及被放在一起研究的一批显现。

intro.en: Phenomenon is the most literal member of the phan- family: a passive participle turned noun, then fitted with English adjective and discipline suffixes.
intro.cn: phenomenon 是 phan- 词族里最字面的成员：一个被动分词变成名词，再装上英语的形容词与学科后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept the Greek participle intact, which is why the English word looks Greek rather than English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊分词原样保留，所以英语词看起来像希腊语而不像英语。

items.meaningCN: 表示“被……的”的被动分词后缀
希腊语中性单数名词词尾
以 -on 结尾名词的希腊式复数词尾

definition_zh: 纽带；联系；债券；结合
definition_en: a strong connection between people
core_image: 两个孩子牵着同一根绳子
scene: 两个孩子一起长大，之间有一种牢固的联结。 A strong bond grew between the two children.
sceneCN: 这里 bond 是「纽带；联系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间的情感连接）；句意是两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。

derivatives.zh: 束缚，奴役
债券持有人

senses.title: A close connection
senses.definition: a strong feeling that connects people
senses.definitionCN: 把人们连在一起的情感
senses.example: A strong bond grew between the two children.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。
senses.why: This comes from the oldest sense of something that ties.
senses.whyCN: 这来自「系住」的最古老含义。

senses.title: A financial certificate
senses.definition: a document promising to repay money with interest
senses.definitionCN: 承诺连本带息偿还的凭证
senses.example: He bought a government bond for his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他把积蓄买了政府债券。
senses.why: A bond ties the lender and the borrower until the money is repaid.
senses.whyCN: 债券把出借人与借款人系在一起，直到还清为止。

senses.title: To join firmly
senses.definition: to stick things together very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把物体牢牢粘合在一起
senses.example: The glue bonds wood to metal.
senses.exampleCN: 这种胶能把木头粘到金属上。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical image of tying two things into one.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了把两物系成一体的具体意象。

intro.en: Bond comes from an Old Norse word for something that ties.
intro.cn: bond 来自古诺尔斯语中表示「系住之物」的词。

items.en: band meant a thing that ties or binds.
items.cn: band 指用来系或捆的东西。

items.en: bond named a rope, a chain and a duty.
items.cn: bond 指绳索、锁链，也指义务。

items.en: a bond became a written promise to pay.
items.cn: bond 成为一种书面的付款承诺。

items.en: chemists spoke of the bond between atoms.
items.cn: 化学家开始用 bond 指原子之间的键。

items.en: bond covers feelings, money and glue.
items.cn: 如今 bond 兼指情感、债券与黏合。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group names ties and links.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示联系与连接的词。

entries.definition: a thin strip that holds things
to tie things together
to make something curved
a connection between people
a connection between two things
a relationship between people or things

normalIntro.en: Bond is a rope you cannot see: it holds people, money and atoms.
normalIntro.cn: bond 是一根看不见的绳：系住人、金钱与原子。

normal.en: Bond and bonds are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 bond，复数是 bonds。

normal.en: A family bond holds people together.
normal.cn: 家庭纽带把人们连在一起。

normal.en: A government bond is a loan to the state.
normal.cn: 政府债券是借给国家的钱。

normal.en: Glue bonds two surfaces.
normal.cn: 胶水把两个表面粘住。

normal.en: Bondage means being tied or trapped.
normal.cn: bondage 意为被束缚或奴役。

abstract.en: See two children holding one rope.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子牵着同一根绳。

abstract.en: See a paper certificate locked in a safe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张锁在保险箱里的凭证。

abstract.en: See two boards pressed together by glue.
abstract.cn: 想象两块木板被胶压在一起。

examples.en: A strong bond grew between the two children.
examples.cn: 两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。

examples.en: He bought a government bond for his savings.
examples.cn: 他把积蓄买了政府债券。

examples.en: The glue bonds wood to metal.
examples.cn: 这种胶能把木头粘到金属上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 bond 想成「绑的」：绑在一起就是联系，借据把人绑住就是债券。

root: bond 源自古诺尔斯语 band，本指用来系捆的东西，中古英语指绳索、锁链与义务，后来发展出债券、化学键与情感纽带等义。

sensesIntro.en: A tie between people, a paper promise to pay, and the act of joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 人与人之间的连接、书面的还款承诺，以及结合的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two children holding the same rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个孩子牵着同一根绳子。

branches.en: a close bond
branches.cn: 紧密的纽带

branches.en: family bonds
branches.cn: 家庭纽带

branches.en: a government bond
branches.cn: 政府债券

branches.en: bond market
branches.cn: 债券市场

branches.en: bond the parts
branches.cn: 把部件黏合

intro.en: Bond takes -age and -holder to name a state and a person.
intro.cn: bond 加 -age 与 -holder 可表示状态与持有者。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old Norse; the items below share the idea of tying.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古诺尔斯语，下面的词都围绕「系住」。

definition_zh: 哭泣；流泪；（伤口）渗液
definition_en: to shed tears because of sadness or strong feeling, and of a wound, to let fluid run out slowly
core_image: 一个人背靠墙坐着，眼泪直往下走，衣襟却一点声音都没有
scene: 散场后影院里只剩一个人，灯亮了，他还坐着，眼睛一点点红起来。 She wept quietly after the film ended, without making a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 weep 是「哭泣」（第 1 个义项：因悲伤或强烈情绪而流泪）；句意为电影结束后她静静地哭，一点声音都没有。靠着墙坐着、眼泪直往下走的人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 哭泣；流泪；（伤口）渗出液体

derivatives.zh: weep 的过去式与过去分词
哭泣的；（枝条）下垂的
哭泣的人；丧服的标志
爱哭的；令人伤感的
无人哀悼的

senses.title: To shed tears
senses.definition: to produce tears from the eyes because of grief or strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤或强烈情绪而从眼中流泪
senses.example: She wept as she read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她读那封信时哭了。
senses.why: This is the core sense, usually quieter and more literary than cry.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，通常比 cry 更静、更书面。

senses.title: To cry for someone or something
senses.definition: to mourn or grieve over a person or event
senses.definitionCN: 为某个人或某件事哀伤
senses.example: They wept for the loss of their old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为失去老师而哭。
senses.why: With for or over the verb names the cause of grief, not just the tears.
senses.whyCN: 接 for 或 over 时，动词指向悲伤的缘由，而不只是眼泪。

senses.title: To cry with joy or relief
senses.definition: to shed tears from an emotion other than grief
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤之外的情绪而流泪
senses.example: Her parents wept with joy at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，她的父母喜极而泣。
senses.why: The tears are the same, so the verb covers any strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 眼泪是一样的，所以这个动词可以覆盖任何强烈的情绪。

senses.title: Of a wound, to run with fluid
senses.definition: of a sore or wound, to discharge liquid slowly
senses.definitionCN: 指疮口或伤口慢慢流出液体
senses.example: The cut on his hand was still weeping.
senses.exampleCN: 他手上的伤口还在渗液。
senses.why: Something that keeps letting drops out looks like a crying eye.
senses.whyCN: 不停滴出东西的物体，像一只流泪的眼睛。

senses.title: To hang downwards
senses.definition: of branches, to droop or hang down, usually in the form weeping
senses.definitionCN: 指枝条下垂，多用 weeping 形式
senses.example: A weeping willow bent over the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 一株垂柳弯在池塘上方。
senses.why: Drooping branches are said to weep, as if they were crying.
senses.whyCN: 下垂的枝条被说成在哭，仿佛它们也在流泪。

intro.en: Weep goes back to Old English wēpan, a Germanic word for crying out and lamenting, and it still carries a quieter, older tone than cry.
intro.cn: weep 可上溯到古英语 wēpan，是日耳曼语中呼喊与哀悼的词，至今仍比 cry 带着更静、更古的意味。

items.en: The root meant to cry out, and related words in other Germanic tongues mean to weep as well.
items.cn: 这一词根意为高声呼喊，其他日耳曼语言中的相关词也表示哭泣。

items.en: Wēpan meant to lament, often aloud, and the strong past wēop became wept.
items.cn: wēpan 意为哀叹，常是出声的，其强变化过去式 wēop 成为 wept。

items.en: The word lost its loud sense while cry took over, and weep settled as the quieter word.
items.cn: 这个词失去了高声义，cry 接替了它，weep 成为更静的用法。

items.en: The wound sense, recorded from the fifteenth century, uses the image of dripping.
items.cn: 伤口义自十五世纪有记录，用的是滴落的意象。

items.en: Weeping willow names a tree whose branches hang like falling tears.
items.cn: weeping willow 指枝条垂落如泪的树。

note.en: The first group shares the weep forms, the second gives the words that sit beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是 weep 的形式与派生，第二组是与它并列的词。

entries.definition: The ordinary past and participle.
entries.definitionCN: weep 的过去式与过去分词

entries.definition: Crying, or hanging down.
A person who weeps, or a hired mourner.
entries.definitionCN: 哭泣的人；雇来的哭丧者

entries.definition: Inclined to cry, or a film that makes one cry.
The everyday word, often louder and with sound.
To cry with short, gasping breaths.
To feel and show deep grief, often publicly.
To cry out with a long, high sound.

normalIntro.en: Weep is the quiet form of crying, and the word also lets a wound and a willow do it.
normalIntro.cn: weep 是哭泣里安静的那种，伤口与柳树也能用它。

normal.en: The past is wept, not weeped.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wept，不是 weeped。

normal.en: Weep over the cause, weep for the person.
normal.cn: weep over 指的是缘由，weep for 指的是那个人。

normal.en: Weep with joy says the tears are glad ones.
normal.cn: weep with joy 说明眼泪是欢喜的。

normal.en: A weeping wound keeps running.
normal.cn: weeping wound 是不断渗液的伤口。

normal.en: A weeping willow is named for its hanging branches.
normal.cn: weeping willow 因垂枝得名。

abstract.en: Picture a face turned away from the light.
abstract.cn: 想一张背过光去的脸。

abstract.en: Feel the line of wet on a collar.
abstract.cn: 感受领口那道湿痕。

abstract.en: Hear no sound at all.
abstract.cn: 听不到一点声音。

examples.en: He wept when he heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到消息时他哭了。

examples.en: The child wept over the broken toy.
examples.cn: 孩子为弄坏的玩具哭了。

examples.en: The sore on his arm had begun to weep.
examples.cn: 他臂上的疮开始渗液。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维普」——维普先生靠墙坐着，眼泪安静地流，一点哭声也没有。

root: 日耳曼语词根（呼喊）→ 古英语 wēpan（哀叹、哭泣，过去式 wēop）→ weep / wept；同源词有 weeping、weepy。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts as quiet tears, widens to grief and to joy, then lends itself to dripping wounds and drooping trees.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从安静的眼泪出发，扩展到悲伤与喜悦，再借给渗液的伤口与下垂的枝条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face against a wall, wet and silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着墙、湿了脸却无声。

branches.en: The tears branch: reading a letter through tears.
branches.cn: 眼泪分支：读信时落泪。

branches.en: The grief and joy branch: mourning a teacher, weeping at good news.
branches.cn: 悲喜分支：哀悼老师，喜极而泣。

branches.en: The wound branch: a cut that keeps running.
branches.cn: 伤口分支：不断渗液的伤口。

branches.en: The tree branch: branches hanging over still water.
branches.cn: 树木分支：垂在静水上的枝条。

branches.en: The tear and wound branch: both are liquid that keeps running.
branches.cn: 泪水与伤口分支：两者都是不停流下的液体。

intro.en: Weep keeps an irregular past and takes -ing, -er and -y in the ordinary way.
intro.cn: weep 保留不规则过去式，并按常规加 -ing、-er 与 -y。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; Latin expressed the same idea with flere, which survives in English borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；拉丁语用 flere 表达同一概念，其痕迹见于英语借词。

definition_zh: 电子；（作定语）电子的；价电子
definition_en: a very small particle with a negative charge that moves around the nucleus of an atom
core_image: 原子中心一颗核，外面几个极小的光点绕着它飞
scene: 示波管里一束细线被磁场轻轻推开，屏幕上留下弯曲的轨迹。 A beam of electrons bends as it passes the magnet.
sceneCN: 这里 electron 是「电子」（第 1 个义项：带负电的亚原子粒子）；句意是一束电子经过磁铁时发生了偏转。

pos.zh: 名词：电子；价电子；（作定语）电子的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「电子的；电子设备的」
由 electronic 加 -s 构成，义为「电子学；电子器件」
由本词与 negative 复合，义为「电负性的」

senses.title: The negative particle
senses.definition: a stable subatomic particle with a negative charge that orbits the nucleus of an atom
senses.definitionCN: 一种带负电、绕原子核运动的稳定亚原子粒子
senses.example: An electron carries a negative charge.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电子带负电荷。
senses.why: When physicists needed a name for the tiny carrier of charge, they reached back to the amber root that had named the force.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家要给电荷的微小载体命名时，又回到了当初为这股力命名的「琥珀」词根。

senses.title: Before a noun as a tool
senses.definition: used before another noun for devices or beams that steer electrons, as in electron microscope
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，指操控电子束的装置，如电子显微镜
senses.example: The lab bought a new electron microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室买了一台新的电子显微镜。
senses.why: The particle became a measuring tool, so its name moved in front of the instrument it drives.
senses.whyCN: 这个粒子成了测量工具，于是它的名字挪到了由它驱动的仪器前面。

senses.title: The electron in a bond
senses.definition: an outer electron that an atom shares or trades when it forms a chemical bond
senses.definitionCN: 原子成键时交出或共享的外层电子
senses.example: Each carbon atom shares four electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 每个碳原子共享四个电子。
senses.why: Chemistry counts only the outermost electrons when it explains bonds, and each one keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 化学在解释成键时只数最外层电子，而每一个仍用同一个名字。

intro.en: Electron revives a Greek word for amber; the modern particle name was proposed at the end of the nineteenth century and confirmed when the particle itself was found.
intro.cn: electron 复活了希腊语里表示「琥珀」的词；这个现代粒子名在十九世纪末被提出，并在粒子本身被发现后得到确认。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, and later also the pale alloy that looked like it.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，后来也指外观相似的淡色合金。

items.en: Latin kept the word as electrum and passed the root into the science of charge.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留作 electrum，并把这个词根传进了研究电荷的科学。

items.en: The adjective electric made the root familiar before the particle had a name.
items.cn: 在粒子得名之前，形容词 electric 已让这个词根为人熟悉。

items.en: The physicist Stoney proposed electron as the name of a unit of charge.
items.cn: 物理学家斯通尼提议用 electron 作为电荷单位的名称。

items.en: Thomson's experiments showed that a real particle carried that charge.
items.cn: 汤姆孙的实验证明真的有一种粒子携带这份电荷。

items.en: The name settled on the particle, and the suffix -ic later produced electronic.
items.cn: 这个名字最终固定给了粒子，而 -ic 词尾后来造出了 electronic。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electric family; the near-meaning group sorts the atom's particles and the charge they carry.
note.cn: 形近组收 electric 词族；近义组区分原子里的几种粒子以及它们携带的电荷。

entries.definition: Of the force, or of a device driven by it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电的；用电的」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling electrons in circuits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的电子工作。

entries.definition: The science of electron control, or the circuits themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电子学；电子器件」。

entries.definition: The energy of moving charges.
A particle in the nucleus with a positive charge; equal and opposite to the electron.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「质子」，位于核内、带正电，与电子电量相等、符号相反。

entries.definition: A particle in the nucleus with no charge at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中子」，位于核内，不带电。

entries.definition: An atom that has gained or lost electrons and so carries a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「离子」，是得失电子后带电的原子。

entries.definition: The property itself that the electron carries, not the particle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电荷」，是电子所携带的性质，而不是粒子本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks shrink the amber word down to a point of charge and then hand it to microscopes and bonds.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把「琥珀」那个词缩小成一个电荷点，再交给显微镜与化学键。

normal.en: Electron is the smallest piece of the amber story.
normal.cn: electron 是琥珀这个故事里最小的一块。

normal.en: Protons sit in the middle; electrons run around them.
normal.cn: 质子坐在正中，电子绕着它们跑。

normal.en: An electron microscope sees with particles, not with light.
normal.cn: 电子显微镜用粒子看东西，而不是用光。

normal.en: Bonds are electron deals: share one, give one away.
normal.cn: 化学键就是电子的交易：共享一个，或送走一个。

normal.en: Electric is the field; electron is the smallest worker in it.
normal.cn: electric 是整片场；electron 是场里最小的那个工人。

abstract.en: Picture a nucleus as a lit lamp and electrons as moths circling it.
abstract.cn: 把原子核想成一盏亮着的灯，电子就是绕着它飞的蛾子。

abstract.en: The same word names one particle and a whole technology built on it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名一种粒子，也命名建立在它之上的整套技术。

abstract.en: Electron is a point of charge; everything electronic is that point multiplied.
abstract.cn: electron 是一个电荷点；一切 electronic 的东西都是这个点的千百倍复制。

examples.en: An electron carries a negative charge.
examples.cn: 一个电子带负电荷。

examples.en: A beam of electrons bends as it passes the magnet.
examples.cn: 一束电子经过磁铁时发生了偏转。

examples.en: Each carbon atom shares four electrons.
examples.cn: 每个碳原子共享四个电子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗来克胀」——原子外那颗极小的光点，绕一圈又一圈

root: 源自希腊语 elektron「琥珀」，经拉丁语 electrum 进入英语的科学词汇；十九世纪末被用来命名带负电的粒子。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electron: the particle, the word used before an instrument's name, and the outer electron counted in bonds.
sensesIntro.cn: electron 的三个义项：粒子本身、放在仪器名前作定语，以及成键时被计数的外层电子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright point circling a heavy nucleus.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个明亮的小点绕着重核旋转。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: the carrier of negative charge.
branches.cn: 粒子线：负电荷的载体。

branches.en: THE TOOL: the same name in front of an instrument.
branches.cn: 工具线：同一个名字被放在仪器前面。

branches.en: THE BOND: the outer electron that chemistry counts.
branches.cn: 成键线：化学所数的外层电子。

branches.en: THE OUTERMOST: the electron that is shared is still the same particle.
branches.cn: 最外层线：被共享的那个电子仍然是同一种粒子。

branches.en: THE BEAM: many electrons lined up become an instrument.
branches.cn: 电子束线：许多电子排齐，就成了一件仪器。

intro.en: Electron is built on the amber root plus the Greek noun ending -on; the same root feeds electric and electronic.
intro.cn: electron 用「琥珀」词根加希腊语名词词尾 -on 构成；同一个词根还养出 electric 与 electronic。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are the recorded forms; electron as a particle name is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 是有记录的形式；作为粒子名的 electron 属于现代造词。

items.example: It names the substance that started it all.
items.exampleCN: 它命名了这一切的起点物质。

items.example: It passed the root on to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词根传给拉丁语。
它让这个词根为人熟悉。
它命名一种亚原子粒子。

items.example: It appears in electron and proton.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 electron 与 proton 中。
